BURSEVI:v10p375/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r1.claim: The chapter is described as eight or nine verses and Meccan.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r1.anchor: والبينة والبرية ثمان أو تسع آيات مكية

BURSEVI:v10p375/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r2.claim: The people of the Book are Jews and Christians; their disbelief is expressed as an event because it began after their prophets.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r2.anchor: {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب} أي اليهود والنصارى وإيراد الصلة فعلا لما أن كفرهم حادث بعد أنبيائهم

BURSEVI:v10p375/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r3.claim: The polytheists are idol worshippers; min is explanatory, not partitive, so the verse does not imply that only some polytheists disbelieved.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r3.anchor: {والمشركين} أي عبدة الأصنام ومن للتبيين لا للتبعيض حتى لا يلزم أن لا يكون بعض المشركين كافرين

BURSEVI:v10p375/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r4.claim: The disbelievers are two groups: scriptural communities and those without a revealed book.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r4.anchor: وذلك أن الكفار كانوا جنسين أهل الكتاب كفرق اليهود والنصارى والمشركين وهم الذين كانوا لا ينسبون إلى كتاب

BURSEVI:v10p375/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r5.claim: They were not abandoning their former state of awaiting truth and believing in the last messenger; the people of the Book repeatedly prayed for victory through him and warned their enemies he would soon come.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r5.anchor: {منفكين} خبر كان أي عما كانوا عليه من الوعيد باتباع الحق والإيمان بالرسول المبعوث في آخر الزمان والعزم على إنجازه وهذا الوعد من أهل الكتاب

BURSEVI:v10p375/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r6.claim: The Jews and Christians told polytheist enemies that the promised prophet’s time was near and that they would defeat them with him; later polytheists may have adopted the expectation after seeing scripturalists prevail.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r6.anchor: كانوا يستفتحون ويقولون اللهم افتح علينا وانصرنا بالنبي المبعوث في

BURSEVI:v10p375/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r7.claim: The polytheists asked people of the Book whether Muhammad was the prophet mentioned in their scriptures, while scripturalists misled them by changing his descriptions.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r7.anchor: كما يشهد به أنهم كانوا يسألونهم عن رسول الله هل هو المذكور في كتبهم وكانوا

BURSEVI:v10p375/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r8.claim: Infikāk means separating after close attachment, like a bone dislocating from its joint; inwardly, they held their promise tightly until the evidence arrived, when they split.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r8.anchor: وانفكاك الشيء من الشيء أن يزايله بعد التحامه كالعظم إذا انفك من مفصله وفيه إشارة إلى كمال وكادة وعدهم أي لم يكونوا مفارقين للوعد المذكور

BURSEVI:v10p375/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r9.claim: The clear proof’s arrival, which they had set as the time to unite upon truth, became instead the time of division and rupture; the present tense reflects the narrated scene.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r9.anchor: {حتى تأتيهم البينة} التي كانوا قد جعلوا إتيانها ميقاتا لاجتماع الكلمة والاتفاق على الحق فجعلوه ميقاتا للانفكاك والافتراق

BURSEVI:v10p375/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375/r10.claim: Al-bayyina is the clear proof, namely the Messenger himself; calling him the proof signals his manifest truth and fulfillment of the two scriptures’ promise.
BURSEVI:v10p375/r10.anchor: والبينة الحجة الواضحة {رسول} بدل من البينة عبر عنه عليه السلام بها للإيذان بغاية ظهور أمره وكونه ذلك الموعود في الكتابين

BURSEVI:v10p379/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p379/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p379/r5.claim: Anas reports that God commanded the Prophet to recite this surah to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb; Ubayy asked whether he had been named, heard yes, and wept when told he was mentioned before the Lord of the worlds.
BURSEVI:v10p379/r5.anchor: قال أو سماني لك قال : نعم ، قال : وقد ذكرت عند رب العالمين قال نعم فذرفت عيناه

QASHANI:98:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:98:1/r1.claim: Disbelievers are veiled either from the religion and path to the Real, as the People of the Book, or from the Real itself, as polytheists; they stay astray until a clear proof comes.
QASHANI:98:1/r1.anchor: حجبوا إما عن الدين وطريق الوصول إلى الحق كأهل الكتاب

QASHANI:98:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:98:1/r2.claim: Jews, Christians, and polytheists once quarrelled while claiming their own religion true, yet agreed to wait for the promised Prophet in their books and follow him; the author compares this to sects awaiting the Mahdi and fears they will react similarly.
QASHANI:98:1/r2.anchor: كانوا يتخاصمون ويتعاندون ويدعي كل حزب حقية ما عليه

QASHANI:98:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:98:1/r3.claim: Their divisions and hostility intensified after the proof arrived: every group imagined the Prophet would validate its own inclination, then became more defiant and spiteful when he did not.
QASHANI:98:1/r3.anchor: ما تفرقوا تفرقا قويا وما اشتد اختلافهم وتعاندهم إلا من بعدما جاءتهم البينة بخروجه

QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r1.claim: The majestic basmala is a means through which sinners seek forgiveness and restoration, the obedient reach God and receive support, the learned gain insight, and the gnostics draw near.
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r1.anchor: بسم الله ' اسم عزيز تتصل إليه المذنبون فغفر لهم وجبرهم : وتوسل إليه المطيعون فوصلهم ونصرهم .

QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r2.claim: The disbelievers would not cease their state of disbelief until the proof, Muhammad, came; scripture had led them to affirm him, but when he was sent they envied and rejected him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r2.anchor: منفكين ) : منتهين عن كفرهم حتى تأتيهم البينة : وهي رسول الله ، أي لم يزالوا مجتمعين

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.claim: Qatada says the disbelievers would persist in their condition until the clear proof arrived: the Messenger reciting purified pages, namely the Qur'an praised in the best terms.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3454/r1.anchor: عن قتادة لم يكن الذين كفروا من اهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين قال : منتهين عما هم فيه حتى تاتيهم البينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r1.claim: The Prophet named the surah by its opening words when he told Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that God commanded him to recite it; Ubayy asked whether he had been named and wept. It is commonly called “Lam yakun” in tafsir and hadith books and in Tunisian Qur’an schools.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r1.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم عن أنس بن مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r2.claim: The surah has six reported titles: al-Qayyimah in many muṣḥafs and some tafsirs, al-Bayyinah in some muṣḥafs, Ahl al-Kitab in Ubayy’s muṣḥaf, al-Bariyyah, and al-Infikak, alongside Lam yakun.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says the better-known position among most commentators is that the surah is Meccan; Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAtaʾ ibn Yasar say it is Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية : الأشهر أنها مكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r4.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi reverses the attribution: most commentators and Ibn ʿAbbas call it Medinan, while Yahya ibn Salam says Meccan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r4.anchor: وعكس القرطبي فنسب القول بأنها مدنية إلى الجمهور وابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r5.speaker: أبو حبة البدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r5.claim: Abu Hubba al-Badri reports Gabriel saying that God commanded the Prophet to recite this surah to Ubayy, who was a Medinan; Ibn Kathir transmits it from Ahmad.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers a Medinan date because the surah repeatedly criticizes the People of the Book and because of Abu Hubba’s report; al-Baghawi, Ibn Kathir, and Jabir ibn Zayd also classify it as Medinan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r6.anchor: وهو الأظهر لكثرة ما فيها من تخطئة أهل الكتاب ولحديث أبي حبة البدري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya argues that the Prophet only engaged the People of the Book in disputation at Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r7.anchor: ابن عطية : إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r8.claim: In the revelation order it is 101st, after al-Talaq and before al-Hashr, placing its revelation around late year three or early year four before the Banu Nadir campaign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p467/r8.anchor: وقد عدت المائة وإحدى في ترتيب النزول نزلت بعد سورة الطلاق وقبل سورة الحشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r1.claim: Most count eight verses in the surah, while the people of Basra count nine.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r2.claim: The surah rebukes polytheists and the People of the Book for rejecting the Quran and Messenger, exposes their inconsistency in rejecting the proof they awaited, refutes their claim that God mandated their existing religions, warns them of punishment, declares disbelievers the worst creation, and praises believers with eternal reward and divine pleasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r2.anchor: توبيخ المشركين وأهلل الكتاب على تكذيبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r4.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r4.claim: Al-Fakhr quotes al-Wahidi calling the opening verse among the Quran’s most difficult in structure and interpretation, saying even leading scholars have floundered; al-Fakhr says he has not yet summarized the problem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r4.anchor: ذكر الفخر عن الواحدي في ( التفسير البسيط ) له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r5.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r5.claim: Al-Fakhr’s apparent reading is that disbelievers would leave disbelief when the proof, the Messenger, came, whereas verse 4 says the People of the Book only split after the proof arrived, apparently worsening their disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r5.anchor: تقتضي أنهم صاروا منفكين عن كفرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r6.claim: On the surface, verse 1’s implied promise that the disbelievers leave unbelief at the Messenger’s coming contradicts verse 4’s statement that the People of the Book divided only after the proof came.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p468/r6.anchor: حصل بين الآية الأولى والآية الثانية مناقضة في الظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r1.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r1.claim: Al-Fakhr’s difficulty assumes “Messenger from God” apposes “the proof” and that the omitted complement of “cease” is disbelief; “until” would then imply they leave disbelief upon the Messenger’s arrival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r1.anchor: لدلالة الكلام عليه لأنهم لما أجريت عليهم صلة الذين كفروا دل ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r3.claim: A further problem is that history shows no disbelievers ever abandoned unbelief, while the subjunctive after “until” signals a future arrival even though the Messenger had come years before this revelation and they persisted in disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r3.anchor: أن المشاهدة دلت على أن الذين كفروا لم ينفكوا عن الكفر في زمن ما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r4.claim: Because the apparent wording and construction fail, the passage must be read nonliterally, either by shifting the sentence’s pragmatic meaning or by shifting a word to metaphor or metonymy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p469/r4.anchor: إما بصرف تركيب الخبر عن ظاهر الإخبار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r1.claim: Exegetes propose about fifteen solutions, which Ibn Ashur groups into five: read the whole sentence as rebuke and astonishment (al-Farraʾ, Naftawayh, al-Zamakhshari); interpret “cease” as leaving divine respite for punishment (Ibn ʿAtiyya); or supply different complements to “cease”—disbelief (ʿAbd al-Jabbar), agreement in disbelief (al-Fakhr, Abu Hayyan), testimony before the mission (Ibn Kaysan al-Asamm), or life itself (some linguists).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r1.anchor: تأويل الجملة بأسرها بأن يؤول الخبر إلى معنى التوبيخ والتعجيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r2.claim: Two further approaches make “until” mean a conditional “even if,” or make the Messenger an angel bringing a heavenly book; the latter is Abu Muslim’s view as reported by al-Fakhr and implies mockery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r2.anchor: بأنه رسول من الملائكة يتلو عليهم صحفا من عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r3.claim: Al-Alusi records most proposed views and al-Qurtubi most of the remainder without attribution; the proposals overlap, so Ibn Ashur says their details can be mapped to his five categories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r3.anchor: وقد تعددت أقوال المفسرين فبلغت بضعة عشر قولا ذكر الآلوسي أكثرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r4.claim: “Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book” means those who disbelieved in Muhammad’s message, as in the verse about the hypocrites’ allies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p470/r4.anchor: أنهم كفروا برسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل ما في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r1.claim: The claim circulated among both groups before the Prophet came, so the future “until the proof comes” fits their former refrain: they would not leave their religion until a promised sign arrived; this prepares for the Messenger described next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r1.anchor: أنهم كانوا يقولون ذلك قبل مجيء الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r2.claim: Here “proof” means the sign they claimed to await, a promised proof from their perspective, not a later event that caused them to abandon disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r2.anchor: أنكم كنتم تقولون لا نترك ما نحن عليه من الدين حتى تأتينا البينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r3.claim: “Infikak” means release or departure, from the transitive verb for separating; its omitted complement is disbelief, supplied by the description of the people as disbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r3.anchor: فالانفكاك : الإقلاع ، وهو مطاوع فكه إذا فصله وفرقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r4.claim: The claim came from Jews in Medina and nearby settlements, passed to Meccan polytheists who consulted them for a defense of rejecting Islam, and also included surrounding Arab tribes and individual Christians.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r4.anchor: فهذا القول صادر من اليهود الذين في المدينة والقرى التي حولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r5.claim: The Quran documents Jews’ claimed condition that they would believe only in a messenger whose sacrifice fire consumed, and their later rejection of a confirming book they already recognized.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r5.anchor: وقد حكى الله عن اليهود أنهم قالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r6.claim: It records Jesus’ prophecy of Ahmad and the Christians’ rejection when he came with clear proofs, as well as the People of the Book’s jealous wish to return believers to disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r6.anchor: وحكى عن النصارى بقوله تعالى حكاية عن عيسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r7.claim: The polytheists likewise rejected the Messenger by demanding signs like those given to earlier messengers or like Moses’ sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p472/r7.anchor: وحكى عن المشركين بقوله : { فلما جاءهم الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r1.claim: The choice of “proof” may translate a phrase from the People of the Book’s scriptures, perhaps Matthew’s “testimony to all nations”; its repetition may reflect that specific resonance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r1.anchor: لعل إيثار التعبير بها هنا لأنها أحسن ما تترجم به العبارة الواقعة في كتب أهل الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r2.claim: The definite “the proof” may be a generic mental definite, functioning like an indefinite “a proof,” as in the expression “enter the market”; Zuhayr’s line similarly uses “war” generically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r2.anchor: تعريف العهد الذهني ، وهو أن يراد معهود بنوعه لا بشخصه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r3.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to the proof familiar to them, their prophets’ promises, though their imagined versions differed; the Quran repeatedly uses this word for the anticipated, clear proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعريف لمعهود عند المخبر عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r4.claim: The partitive “min” in “among the People of the Book” explains which disbelievers are meant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r4.anchor: و { من } في قوله : { من أهل الكتاب } بيانية بيان للذين كفروا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r5.claim: The People of the Book precede the polytheists despite the latter’s graver disbelief because they had priority in circulating the anticipated-proof argument and gave a more learned denial of Muhammad’s prophethood; unlettered polytheists sought their counterarguments, especially after the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p474/r5.anchor: فلما صدمتهم الدعوة المحمدية فزعوا إلى اليهود ليتلقوا منهم ما يردون به تلك الدعوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r1.claim: Ubayy’s reading begins with ‘Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not…’ using kana instead of yakun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r2.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud’s reading places the polytheists before the People of the Book.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r3.claim: Munfakkin means separated or divided; it is not the defective verb ma انفك, which belongs to the sisters of kana.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r4.claim: Mujahid and others say the disbelievers would not leave unbelief and error until the clear proof came; the future verb is used in place of the past because the rest of the verse describes what had not yet happened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r4.anchor: لم يكونوا منفكين عن الكفر والضلال حتى جاءتهم البينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r5.claim: Al-Farra’ and others say they remained aware of Muhammad’s prophethood and awaiting his appearance, then divided after the proof came.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r5.anchor: لم يكونوا منفكين عن معرفة صحة نبوة محمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r6.claim: Some grammarians treat the negation plus munfakkin as the kana construction, supplying a predicate such as ‘knowing Muhammad’s affair.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r6.anchor: وذهب بعض النحويين إلى هذا النفي المتقدم مع منفكين يجعلها تلك التي هي مع كان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r7.claim: The author prefers a third sense: the people remained under God’s care and power until He sent a warning messenger, establishing proof and completing the blessing for believers, as in other Qur’anic passages.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r7.anchor: أن يكون المراد لم يكن هؤلاء القوم منفكين من أمر الله تعالى وقدرته ونظره لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#3/r8.claim: Some recite al-mushrikun in the nominative, while the majority read al-mushrikin in the genitive; the author says their meanings are clear.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r1.claim: The clear proof means the evident account, namely Muhammad; most readers put rasul in the nominative, while Ubayy reads rasulan in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r6.claim: The majority say Sura al-Bayyina is Medinan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r7.claim: Another view says the surah is Meccan, reported by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas and chosen by Yahya ibn Salam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p194/r7.anchor: والثاني مكية قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس واختاره يحيى بن سلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r1.claim: The people of the Book are Jews and Christians, and the polytheists are idol worshippers; munfakkīn means separated or departed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r1.anchor: يعني اليهود والنصارى والمشركين أي ومن المشركين وهم عبدة الأوثان منفكين أي منفصلين وزائلين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r2.claim: Although the verse uses a future form, it means that they did not leave their disbelief until the proof came, namely Muhammad, who clarified their error; this rescued believers among both groups.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r2.anchor: لم يكونوا زائلين عن كفرهم وشركهم حتى تأتيهم أي حتى أتتهم فلفظه لفظ المستقبل ومعناه الماضي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r3.claim: Some exegetes say the groups did not disagree about God sending a prophet until He sent one, after which they split.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r3.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن معنى الآية لم يختلفوا أن الله يبعث إليهم نبياحتى بعث فافترقوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they would not leave their state without God's proofs until the clear proof had been established against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين عن حجج الله حتى أقيمت عليهم البينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196/r5.claim: The author prefers the first interpretation: they remained in disbelief until the Messenger came.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r1.speaker: أبو حية البدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r1.claim: Abu Hayya reports that Gabriel told the Prophet God commanded him to teach this surah to Ubayy; Ubayy asked whether he was mentioned, heard yes, and wept.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا حية البدري -وهو: مالك بن عمرو بن ثابت الأنصاري-قال: لما نزلت: " لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب " إلى آخرها، قال جبريل:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet told Ubayy that God had commanded him to recite the opening of this surah to him and had named him; Ubayy wept.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب: "إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك: " لم يكن الذين كفروا "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r3.claim: Ubayy reports that, while the Prophet recited the surah to him, he also recited that Adam’s insatiable desire for wealth ends only with dust and that the true religion is upright, non-associating devotion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p454/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إني أمرت أن أقرأ عليك سورة كذا وكذا".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls al-Tabarani’s report about the Prophet offering to recite the Qur’an to Ubayy strange by this route and says the earlier versions are established.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r1.anchor: هذا غريب من هذا الوجه، والثابت ما تقدم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r1.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are worshippers of idols and fire, Arabs and non-Arabs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r1.anchor: أما أهل الكتاب فهم: اليهود والنصارى، والمشركون: عبدة الأوثان والنيران،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r2.claim: Mujahid, followed by Qatadah, glosses the unbelievers’ not being free from their state as their not ceasing until the truth became clear to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لم يكونوا {منفكين} يعني: منتهين حتى يتبين لهم الحق. وكذا قال قتادة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the clear proof as the Qur’an and its messenger Muhammad, who recites it from purified heavenly scriptures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r3.anchor: أي: هذا القرآن؛ ولهذا قال تعالى:

FARRA:v3p281/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p281/r1.claim: One interpretation takes munfakkīn as “coming to an end” until Muḥammad and the Qur’an arrived as clear proof.
FARRA:v3p281/r1.anchor: وأهل الكتاب منفكين» . فقد اختلف التفسير، فقيل: لم يكونوا منفكين منتهين حتى

FARRA:v3p281/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p281/r2.claim: Another says they did not abandon the scriptural description of Muḥammad as prophet until he appeared; then they split, as verse 4 confirms.
FARRA:v3p281/r2.anchor: والقرآن. وقال آخرون: لم يكونوا تاركين لصفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

FARRA:v3p281/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p281/r3.claim: Infikāk can mean continuing, which takes negation and a verb, or separation, which can occur without either.
FARRA:v3p281/r3.anchor: فإذا كانت على جهة يزال فلا بد لها من فعل، وأن يكون معها جحد، فتقول: ما انفككت أذكرك،

FARRA:v3p281/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
FARRA:v3p281/r4.claim: Dhū al-Rumma’s verse says the camels never separate except while resting, using illā with the sense of separation rather than “continue.”
FARRA:v3p281/r4.anchor:
وقد قال ذو الرمة:
قلائص لا تنفك إلا مناخة ... على الخسف أو ترمي بها بلدا قفرا

FARRA:v3p281/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p281/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p281/r5.claim: The verse’s illā is compatible with separation but not with the “I have continued” sense, since one cannot say “I continued except standing.”
FARRA:v3p281/r5.anchor: ينوي بها التمام وخلاف: يزال، لأنك لا تقول: ما زلت إلا قائما.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#2/r1.claim: Munfakkīn means departing or ceasing; mā anfakku fī kadhā means “they continue in such a state.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#2/r1.anchor: {منفكين} زائلين (2) . يقال: ما أنفك في كذا؛ أي لا أزال.

JISHUMI:v10p7495/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r1.claim: The surah is also called al-Qayyima, is reportedly Medinan, and has seven verses in the Basran count but eight elsewhere.
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r1.anchor:
وتسمى سورة (القيمة)
وهي مدنية فيما روي.
وهي سبع آيات في البصري، وثماني آيات في غيره.

JISHUMI:v10p7495/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r2.speaker: أبي عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r2.claim: Whoever recites Sūrat Lam Yakun will be with the best of creation on Resurrection Day.
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r2.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: من قرأ سورة (لم يكن) كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية

JISHUMI:v10p7495/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r3.speaker: أنس عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r3.claim: The Prophet told Ubayy that God had ordered him to recite Lam Yakun to him; when Ubayy asked if named, the Prophet said yes, and Ubayy wept.
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r3.anchor: وعن أنس، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال لأبي بن كعب: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ [عليك] (لم يكن الذين كفروا)،

JISHUMI:v10p7495/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r4.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports that people would abandon family and property to learn the surah if they knew what it contained.
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r4.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: لو يعلم الناس ما في هذه السورة (لم يكن الذين كفروا) لعطلوا الأهل والمال وتعلموها.

JISHUMI:v10p7495/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r5.claim: Since al-Qadr showed the Qur'an's descent as proof for humanity, this surah opens by saying earlier unbelievers were not without proofs.
JISHUMI:v10p7495/r5.anchor: ولما بين في سورة (القدر) إنزال القرآن حجة على الخلق، افتتح هذه السورة بأن الكفار قبله لم يكونوا خالين عن الحجج.

JISHUMI:v10p7496/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r3.speaker: الأعمش
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r3.claim: The common reading has al-mushrikīn in the genitive coordinated with People of the Book; al-Aʿmash raises it in coordination with “those who disbelieved,” and Ibn Masʿūd's codex is reported to reorder the phrase.
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r3.anchor: قراءة العامة: المشركين بالياء في موضع الجر عطفا على (أهل الكتاب)، وقرأ الأعمش: والمشركون رفعا

JISHUMI:v10p7496/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r5.claim: Infikāk means separation after close joining and is often negated like mā zāla; it may mean continuity and require a negative plus predicate, or separation without those requirements.
JISHUMI:v10p7496/r5.anchor: الانفكاك: الانفصال عن شدة اجتماع، وأكثر ما يستعمل في النفي كما أن (ما زال) كذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r1.claim: Bayyina is an evident proof that distinguishes truth from falsehood; its root connotes separation and making something clear.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r1.anchor: والبينة: الحجة الظاهرة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل، وأصله من البينونة،

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r9.claim: The People of the Book mean Jews and Christians who claim Torah and Gospel despite their distortion; the polytheists are idolaters, especially bookless Arabs.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r9.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى؛ لأن لهم كتابا يعتزون إليه وإن كان محرفا

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r10.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r10.claim: One meaning is that unbelievers were never left without God's proofs; evidences continually came to them and established the case.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r10.anchor: لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين من حجج الله وبيناته حتى تأتيهم من قبل الله البينة

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان والفراء
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r11.claim: Another view says they retained the Prophet's description in their scriptures until his mission, then split, disbelieved, and denied him.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r11.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن هؤلاء الكفار تاركين لصفة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وأنه في كتابهم حتى بعث،

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r12.claim: The phrase may target obstinate deniers who knew the Messenger's truth but demanded further proofs in defiance; the ensuing messenger and purified pages make the proof clear.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r12.anchor: وقيل: المراد من الفرقتين المعاندون الذين عرفوا صدق الرسول وصحة ما جاء به، وكفروا وعاندوا، وطلبوا زيادة الأدلة إعناتا،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r1.claim: Before Muhammad's mission, both People of the Book and idolaters said they would retain their religion until the promised prophet named in Torah and Gospel came.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r1.anchor: كان الكفار من الفريقين أهل الكتاب وعبدة الأصنام يقولون قبل مبعث النبي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r2.claim: They expected the Messenger to unite them on truth, but his arrival further separated them; this recalls the sinner who worsens after getting the wealth he claimed to await.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r2.anchor: ثم ما فرقهم عن الحق ولا أقرهم على الكفر إلا مجيء الرسول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r3.claim: Infikak means separating from something fused together, like a bone dislocated from its joint; they remained attached to religion until the proof arrived.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r3.anchor: وانفكاك الشيء من الشيء . أن يزايله بعد التحامه به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r4.claim: The clear proof is the Messenger; Abdullah's reading treats “messenger” as a circumstantial description of the proof.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r4.anchor: و { البينة } الحجة الواضحة . و { رسول } بدل من البينة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r6.claim: Their scattering means departing from truth or splitting into believers, deniers, and those who recognized truth but resisted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r6.anchor: أو تفرقهم فرقا ؛ فمنهم من آمن ، ومنهم من أنكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r7.claim: The verse first groups scripturalists with idolaters, then singles out scripturalists because they knew the Messenger from scripture, making their separation worse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p788/r7.anchor: لأنهم كانوا على علم به لوجوده في كتبهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p789/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p789/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p789/r1.claim: A report says one who recites Lam Yakun will be with the best of creation on the Day of Resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p789/r1.anchor: من قرأ لم يكن كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية

MAJAZ:v2p306/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p306/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p306/r1.claim: Munfakkīn means departing or ceasing, until the clear proof comes to them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam classifies Surat al-Bayyina as Meccan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r1.anchor: مكية في قول يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r2.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315/r2.claim: The majority classify it as Medinan, and the author says this is correct.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r1.claim: Those disbelieving among the People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are idol-worshipping Arabs and others without a scripture.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r1.anchor: معناه لم يكن الذين كفروا من اليهود والنصارى الذين هم أهل الكتاب , ولم يكن المشركون الذين هم عبدة الأوثان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r2.claim: One interpretation of munfakkin is that they would not stop associating partners with God until the truth became clear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : لم يكونوا منتهين عن الشرك { حتى تأتيهم البينة } حتى يتبين لهم الحق .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r3.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r3.claim: Al-Rabi says they remained in shirk and doubt until the proof, meaning messengers, came.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r3.anchor: وهذا قول ثان : لم يزالوا مقيمين على الشرك والريبة حتى تأتيهم البينة , يعنى الرسل , قاله الربيع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r4.claim: Ibn Isa says they had agreed God would send a messenger, but split when Muhammad came, with some believing and others disbelieving.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r4.anchor: لم يفترقوا ولم يختلفوا أن الله سيبعث إليهم رسولا حتى بعث الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم وتفرقوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r5.claim: A fourth interpretation is that they could not be left without God's arguments until a proof established the case against them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r5.anchor: الرابع : لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين من حجج الله تعالى , حتى تأتيهم البينة التي تقوم بها عليهم الحجة , قال امرؤ القيس :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r6.speaker: امرؤ القيس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r6.claim: A line by Imru al-Qays attests to anfakka meaning to become free or break away from something.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#2/r6.anchor: التي تقوم بها عليهم الحجة , قال امرؤ القيس :

MUJAHID:v2p774/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p774/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p774/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses munfakkin as ceasing or ending: they would not believe until the truth was made clear to them.
MUJAHID:v2p774/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ منفكين ﴾ يعني منتهين يقول لم يكونوا ليؤمنوا حتى يتبين لهم الحق

MUQATIL:98:1-6/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r1.claim: People of the Book means Jews and Christians, the polytheists are Arab idolaters, and remaining apart means ceasing from disbelief and polytheism; the clear proof is Muhammad, who explains their error.
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r1.anchor: { منفكين } يعني منتهين عن الكفر والشرك

MUQATIL:98:1-6/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r2.claim: The People of the Book asked when the messenger they found described in their scripture would be raised, while the Arabs said they would be sincere worshippers if they had a reminder from earlier peoples.
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r2.anchor: أهل الكتاب قالوا: متى يبعث الذي نجده في كتابنا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r1.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are idol worshippers, and the clear proof is Muhammad, whose coming ended their prior persistence in disbelief, though some believed and others remained disbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r1.anchor: والمراد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لم يتركوا كفرهم حتى يبعث محمد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r2.claim: Munfakkīn means separated from disbelief; the omitted object is understood from the relative phrase alladhīna kafarū.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r2.anchor: منفصلين عن الكفر وحذف لأن صلة الذين تدل عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r3.claim: Ahl al-rajul means those closest to him, while Ahl al-Islam denotes those who profess Islam.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351/r3.anchor: وأهل الرجل أخص الناس به وأهل الإسلام من يدين به

NAHHAS:v5p271/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p271/r1.claim: Lam yakun is jussive; the nūn loses its ḍamma and the wāw drops at two adjacent sukūns despite the nūn's temporary vowel.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r1.anchor: يكن في موضع جزم بلم وعلامة الجزم فيه حذف الضمة من النون وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v5p271/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p271/r2.claim: Do not follow the account that both wāw and ḍamma were deleted by jussive marking; the movement is only temporary.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r2.anchor: ولا تعرج على قول من قال حذفت الواو والضمة للجزم ولا يجوز عند الخليل وسيبويه

NAHHAS:v5p271/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r3.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه والكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v5p271/r3.claim: Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī, and al-Farrāʾ reject dropping the nūn in lam yakun after its vowel has become mobile.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز عند الخليل وسيبويه والكسائي والفراء حذف النون على لغة من قال لم يك زيد جالسا

NAHHAS:v5p271/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r4.speaker: غيرهم
NAHHAS:v5p271/r4.claim: Other grammarians allow loss of the nūn and cite a poem saying wa-lāk isqunī.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r4.anchor: وأجاز غيرهم حذفها كما قال ( ولاك اسقني إن كان ماؤك ذا فضل )

NAHHAS:v5p271/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p271/r5.claim: Al-mushrikīn is coordinated with ahl; if it coordinated with alladhīna, it would be nominative.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r5.anchor: والمشركين عطف على أهل ولو كان عطفا على الذين لكان مرفوعا

NAHHAS:v5p271/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r6.speaker: عطاء
NAHHAS:v5p271/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says munfakkīn means departing or ceasing, like bariḥa and zāla.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r6.anchor: منفكين خبر يكن في معناه قولان قال عطاء منفكين بارحين وبرح وزال في منهاج واحد

NAHHAS:v5p271/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r7.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p271/r7.claim: Another interpreter says munfakkīn means divided or separated.

NAHHAS:v5p271/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p271/r9.claim: The separation reading is linguistically preferable: if munfakkīn meant ceasing, kāna would need a predicate; infaqqa means one thing separated from another.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r9.anchor: وهذا القول في العربية أولى لأن منفكين لو كان بمعنى زائلين لاحتاج إلى خبر

NAHHAS:v5p271/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r10.speaker: ذو الرمة
NAHHAS:v5p271/r10.claim: Dhu al-Rummah's poem ma tanfakku illā munākhah is cited for tanfakku meaning separate from, with munākhah as a detached exception.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r10.anchor:
كما قال ذو الرمة
( قلائص ما تنفك إلا مناخة

NAHHAS:v5p271/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r11.speaker: الأصمعي
NAHHAS:v5p271/r11.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says Dhu al-Rummah erred because he understood mā tanfakku as mā tazālu, 'continues to be.'
NAHHAS:v5p271/r11.anchor: وزعم الأصمعي أن ذا الرمة أخطأ في هذا قال أبو جعفر تأول الأصمعي ما تنفك ما تزال

NAHHAS:v5p271/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r12.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v5p271/r12.claim: Al-Māzinī says al-Aṣmaʿī was wrong: the clause ma tanfakku is complete before the detached exception illā munākhah.
NAHHAS:v5p271/r12.anchor: والصواب ما قال المازني قال أخطأ الأصمعي وما تنفك كلام تام ثم قال إلا مناخة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r1.claim: The common reading matches the written codex; Ibn Masud's wording is an explanatory reading, not recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r1.anchor: كذا قراءة العامة، وخط المصحف. وقرأ ابن مسعود «لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين» وهذه قراءة على التفسير

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi allows Ibn Masud's wording as clarification but not liturgical recitation, since recitation follows the codex; he cites a Prophetic explanatory rendering of divorce verse 1.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r2.anchor: ابن العربي: « وهي جائزة في معرض البيان، لا في معرض التلاوة فقد قرأ النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r3.claim: People of the Book means Jews and Christians; the word for polytheists is grammatically genitive, coordinated with People of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r3.anchor: من أهل الكتاب } يعني اليهود والنصارى. { والمشركين } في موضع جر عطفا على «أهل الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the People of the Book as the Jews of Yathrib, especially Qurayza, Nadir, and Qaynuqa, and the polytheists as the Meccan and surrounding idolaters, including Quraysh.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r4.anchor: ابن عباس: «أهل الكتاب»: اليهود الذين كانوا بيثرب، وهم قريظة والنضير وبنو قينقاع. والمشركون: الذين كانوا بمكة وحولها

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r5.claim: Munfakkin can mean ceasing and turning away from disbelief.

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the phrase to mean reaching their life's end and dying before the proof came; on this reading infikak means reaching the limit.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r6.anchor: الانتهاء بلوغ الغاية أي لم يكونوا ليبلغوا نهاية أعمارهم فيموتوا، حتى تأتيهم البينة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r7.claim: A further interpretation makes munfakkin mean vanishing: their appointed duration would not disappear before a messenger came.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r7.anchor: منفكين } زائلين أي لم تكن مدتهم لتزول حتى يأتيهم رسول

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r8.claim: Arabic usage ma انفككت أفعل كذا and ma انفك قائما means continuing to do something or remaining standing; the root fakk means opening, as when opening a book or unfastening a bracelet.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r8.anchor: ما انفككت أفعل كذا: أي ما زلت. وما انفك فلان قائما: أي ما زال قائما. وأصل الفك: الفتح

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r9.speaker: طرفة
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r9.claim: Tarafa's verse uses infikak for not ceasing, with a sword described as clinging at the speaker's waist.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r9.anchor:
طرفة:
فآليت لا ينفك كشحي بطانة
لعضب رقيق الشفرتين مهند

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r10.speaker: ذو الرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r10.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse uses the verb for camels that do not cease to be stationed, with illa added.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r10.anchor:
ذو الرمة:
حراجيج ما تنفك إلا مناخة
على الخسف أو نرمي بها بلدا قفرا

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r11.claim: Some gloss munfakkin as departing: they would not leave this world until the proof came.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r11.anchor: منفكين»: بارحين أي لم يكونوا ليبرحوا ويفارقوا الدنيا، حتى تأتيهم البينة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r12.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r12.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the People of the Book kept Muhammad's description in their scriptures until he was sent, then envied and denied him, as in 2:89; the polytheists likewise praised him as trustworthy until the proof came and they became hostile.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r12.anchor: ابن كيسان: أي لم يكن أهل الكتاب تاركين صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في كتابهم، حتى بعث فلما بعث

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r13.claim: Some linguists derive munfakkin from a childbirth separation that fails to heal and causes death, so the verse means people are not punished or destroyed until messengers and scriptures establish proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1/r13.anchor: أنفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة وهو أن ينفصل، فلا يلتئم فتهلك. المعنى: لم يكونوا معذبين ولا هالكين إلا بعد قيام الحجة

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r1.claim: One explanation counts the People of the Book among the polytheists: Christians are Trinitarian and most Jews anthropomorphists, so both groups share shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r1.anchor: فالنصارى مثلثة، وعامة اليهود مشبهة والكل شرك

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r2.claim: Another view takes kufr as rejection of Muhammad: the People of the Book are rejecting Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are idolaters without a scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r2.anchor: ولم يكن المشركون الذين هم عبدة الأوثان من العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r3.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r3.claim: Al-Qushayri finds that interpretation unlikely because the proof is a messenger, apparently Muhammad, so it would be odd to say Muhammad-deniers persisted until Muhammad came; he allows that some formerly revered him and believed when his signs came.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r3.anchor: القشيري: وفيه بعد لأن الظاهر من قوله: { حتى تأتيهم البينة * رسول من الله } أن هذا الرسول هو محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r4.claim: Al-A'mash and Ibrahim read al-mushrikun in the nominative; Qurtubi prefers the common reading because nominative coordination makes both groups seem outside the People of the Book.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وإبراهيم «والمشركون» رفعا، عطفا على «الذين والقراءة الأولى أبين لأن الرفع يصير فيه الصنفان كأنهم من غير أهل الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r5.claim: Ubayy's codex reads fa-ma kana and Ibn Masud's codex reads the explanatory ordering, both recorded as alternate written forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r5.anchor: وفي حرف أبي: «فما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركون منفكين». وفي مصحف ابن مسعود: «لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين

QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r6.claim: The proof may be read as having come; it is Muhammad, the messenger sent by God.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:1-2/r6.anchor: رسول من الله } أي بعيث من الله جل ثناؤه

QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r1.claim: The surah is Madinan according to most reports, though some say Meccan; Qutb favors Madinan on the basis of reports and its declarative style but does not rule out a Meccan origin.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r1.anchor: فإن كونها مكية لا يمكن استبعاده

QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r2.claim: Mention of the People of the Book and zakah does not exclude a Meccan origin: some People of the Book lived in Mecca, Najran Christians visited and believed, and zakah appears in Meccan surahs.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r2.anchor: وذكر الزكاة فيها وذكر أهل الكتاب لا يعتبر قرينة مانعة

QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r3.claim: The surah's four central truths are that the final Messenger's mission was necessary, the People of the Book divided after proof, religion's core is simple and one, and the disbelievers and believers face different fates.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r3.anchor: كانت ضرورية لتحويل الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب

QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r4.claim: The earth had become deeply corrupt, with both scriptural communities having distorted earlier religions and polytheism widespread; only a new message, method, and movement could bring reform.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r4.anchor: لقد كانت الأرض في حاجة ماسة إلى رسالة جديدة كان الفساد قد عم أرجاءها كلها بحيث لا يرتجى لها صلاح إلا برسالة جديدة

QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r5.claim: Those disbelievers would not abandon their condition without the new message and a Messenger who himself served as a decisive, clear proof.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:1/r5.anchor: وما كانوا لينفكوا ويتحولوا عن هذا الكفر الذي صاروا إليه إلا بهذه الرسالة الجديدة

RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's explanation, preferred by Razi, resolves the apparent contradiction: verse 98:1 reports disbelievers saying they would leave their religion only when the promised Prophet came, while 98:4 reports that his arrival actually divided them from truth.

RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r2.claim: Al-Qāḍī removes the conflict by reading the sense as they would not abandon disbelief even when the proof came; Razi rejects this because حتى does not mean that in Arabic.
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r2.anchor: هكذا ذكره القاضي إلا أن تفسير لفظة حتى بهذا ليس من اللغة في شيء

RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r3.speaker: ابن عرفة
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿArafa reads انفكاك as ceasing to praise Muhammad: before his coming they mentioned his virtues, but after he came they split into hostile claims; the imperfect can carry past meaning, as in 2:102 and 2:89.
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عرفة : أي حتى أتتهم ، فاللفظ لفظ المضارع ومعناه الماضي

RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says the whole group remained in disbelief until the Messenger came; afterward the group changed because some believed and others remained disbelievers, satisfying حتى.
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r4.anchor: كفى ذلك في العمل بمدلول لفظ حتى

RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r5.claim: A further view says they were previously certain of their inherited religions, but Muhammad's coming unsettled their convictions and left them doubtful about their own and other religions; Razi compares this to humanity before prophetic missions.
RAZI-FULL:v32p37#2/r5.anchor: كانوا قبل مبعث الرسول منفكين عن التردد في كفرهم بل كانوا جازمين به معتقدين حقيقته

RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r1.claim: The disbelievers comprise two groups: scriptural communities, including Jews and Christians who altered their religion and scripture, and polytheists with no scripture.
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r1.anchor: الكفار كانوا جنسين أحدهما : أهل الكتاب كفرق اليهود والنصارى

RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r2.claim: To explain من, one view takes it as explanatory, like the phrase about avoiding the abomination of idols in 22:30.
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r2.anchor: كلمة من ههنا ليست للتبعيض بل للتبيين كقوله : { فاجتنبوا الرجس من الاوثان }

RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r3.claim: Another view says those rejecting Muhammad include some People of the Book: Christians' trinitarianism and Jews' anthropomorphism are forms of shirk; several coordinated descriptions can name one group, as in 9:112.
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r3.anchor: بعضهم من أهل الكتاب ، وذلك لأن النصارى مثلثة واليهود عامتهم مشبهة

RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r4.claim: Some scholars include Zoroastrians among scriptural communities, citing a prophetic instruction to treat them by the People of the Book's rule; others exclude them because the verse concerns Arabian Jews and Christians, as in 6:156.
RAZI-FULL:v32p38/r4.anchor: ذكر بعض العلماء أنهم داخلون في أهل الكتاب لقوله عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r1.claim: Though واو gives no sequence, People of the Book come first because the surah is Medinan, they knew scripture and could best recognize Muhammad, their persistence was more blameworthy, and others followed their example.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r1.anchor: أن السورة مدنية فكأن أهل الكتاب هم المقصودون بالذكر

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r2.claim: Calling them People of the Book rather than Jews and Christians highlights their learning, which can honor them or intensify their culpability and punishment for disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r2.anchor: لأن كونه عالما يقتضي مزيد قبح في كفره

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r3.claim: Some jurists infer that all disbelief is one religion, so a polytheist may inherit from a Jew and vice versa, because the verse places both under disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r3.anchor: قال العلماء : الكفر كله ملة واحدة ، فالمشرك يرث اليهودي وبالعكس

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r4.claim: Others infer from the conjunction that the categories differ: a protected scripturalist is not a polytheist, consistent with the reported distinction concerning marriage and slaughtered food.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r4.anchor: أن العطف أوجب المغايرة ، فلذلك نقول : الذمي ليس بمشرك

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r5.claim: Naming People of the Book warns against trusting learned people, since Quran scholars can repeat the failures of earlier communities.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r5.anchor: نبه بذكر أهل الكتاب أنه لا يجوز الاغترار بأهل العلم إذ قد حدث في أهل القرآن مثل ما حدث

RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r6.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl derives انفكاك from opening or removing a bond: release follows close attachment; thus disbelievers clung strongly to their religion until the evident proof came, and bayyina is proof separating truth from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v32p39/r6.anchor: الانفكاك هو انفراج الشيء عن الشيء وأصله من الفك وهو الفتح والزوال

RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r1.claim: Those identifying the proof as Muhammad say his extraordinary seriousness in proclaiming prophethood rules out fabrication and mental deficiency, while the totality of his qualities reaches miraculous perfection, as al-Jāḥiẓ and al-Ghazālī argued.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r1.anchor: أن ذاته كانت بينة على نبوته

RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r2.claim: A further argument is that Muhammad's numerous, manifest miracles make him himself a proof; God accordingly calls him a shining lamp in 33:46.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r2.anchor: أن معجزاته عليه الصلاة والسلام كانت في غاية الظهور وكانت أيضا في غاية الكثرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r3.claim: The next phrase رسول من الله is grammatically taken as an appositive to البينة; ʿAbd Allāh reads رسولا as a circumstantial accusative.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r3.anchor: فهو رفع على البدن من البينة

RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r4.claim: The definite article in البينة identifies the Prophet foretold in the Torah and Gospel, or magnifies him as the ultimate proof; the indefinite رسول then adds emphasis by naming him as a messenger of exceptional stature.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r4.anchor: والألف واللام في قوله : { البينة } للتعريف أي هو الذي سبق ذكره

RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r5.claim: Abū Muslim says the proof means messengers from God who recite purified sheets, as in the request for a heavenly book and for unfolded pages.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40/r5.anchor: وهو قول أبي مسلم قال : المراد من قوله : / { حتى تأتيهم البينة }

RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd take the proof as the Quran, citing 20:133; رسول من الله then has an omitted noun, meaning that proof is revelation and the Messenger recites purified sheets.
RAZI-FULL:v32p40#2/r1.anchor: القول الثالث : وهو قتادة وابن زيد : { البينة } هي القرآن

SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r1.claim: Min ahl al-kitāb is an omitted modifier of the subject alladhīna kafarū.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r1.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف، لأنه حال من فاعل " كفروا

SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r2.claim: The common accusative/genitive form al-mushrikīn coordinates with ahl and divides unbelievers into People of the Book and polytheists; a nominative reading coordinates with alladhīna kafarū.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r2.anchor: العامة على قراءة " المشركين " بالياء عطفا على " أهل " قسم الكافرين إلى صنفين

SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r3.claim: The author treats munfakkīn as predicate of kāna, with infakka complete here and needing no predicate; another view makes it incomplete with an understood predicate, knowing Muhammad's affair.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r3.anchor: منفكين } خبر يكون. ومنفكين اسم فاعل من انفك. وهي هنا التامة، فلذلك لم يحتج إلى خبر

SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r4.claim: The interlocutor says omitting a predicate of kāna is impossible except by ellipsis for necessity, citing poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r4.anchor: وحذف خبر كان [وأخواتها] لا يجوز اقتصارا ولا اختصارا

SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r5.claim: The author challenges the interlocutor's logic: both objects of ẓanna can be omitted or one omitted despite serving as predicate and governed object, while omission by اقتصار remains disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1/r5.anchor: وهذا منتقض بمعفولي " ظن " فإن كلا منهما فيه المعنيان المذكوران، ومع ذلك يحذفان

SAMIN-DURR:98:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:1#2/r1.claim: Ḥattā taʾtiyahum attaches either to lam yakun or to munfakkīn.
SAMIN-DURR:98:1#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { حتى تأتيهم }: متعلقة ب " لم يكن " أو ب " منفكين ".

STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r1.speaker: many commentators; others
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r1.claim: Many classify al-Bayyinah as Madinan, while others regard it as Makkan; it is named for the clear proof and also called lam yakun and al-Qiyāmah.
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r1.anchor: any commentators take al-Bayyinah to be a Madinan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r2.claim: Bayyinah derives from bayyana, meaning to make or become clear; Quranic clarity marks revelation and prophetic teaching and distinguishes truth from concealment and caprice.
STUDYQURAN:98:intro/r2.anchor: Bayyinah derives from the verb bayyana, meaning “to make or to become clear, evident, manifest, plain, or apparent,”

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r1.speaker: Sh, W
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r1.claim: Some commentators regard this as one of the Qur’an’s most difficult verses.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r1.anchor: Some commentators consider this verse to be among the most difficult verses of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r2.speaker: Bḍ, IK, Q, Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r2.claim: Most commentators say the disbelievers among the People of the Book include both Jews and Christians.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r2.anchor: According to most commentators, those who disbelieve among the People of the Book refers to disbelievers among both Jews and Christians

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r3.claim: A minority identifies the People of the Book here only as the Jews of Medina.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r3.anchor: though some say it refers only to the Jews of Madinah

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r4.speaker: Q, R, Sh, Z
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r4.claim: The majority understand the verse to mean that disbelievers persist in disbelief until revelation’s clear proof arrives.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r4.anchor: Most read this verse to mean that disbelievers will not leave their disbelief until the clear proof of revelation has come to them

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r5.speaker: Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r5.claim: Another reading is that people will not be punished or destroyed before revelation brings them proof; the idolaters are not abandoned but tested by their response.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r5.anchor: they will not be punished or destroyed until the proof of revelation has been brought to them

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r6.claim: This reading fits the principle that God sends truth through a messenger before punishing people for wrong belief and may concern rejection of Muhammad’s prophethood rather than God’s existence.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r6.anchor: God will not punish any for wrong belief until they have been presented with the truth and then rejected it

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r7.speaker: Q, R, Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r7.claim: Most commentators identify the clear proof as the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r7.anchor: Most interpret the clear proof as a reference to the Quran

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r8.speaker: Q, R, Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r8.claim: Others identify the clear proof as the Prophet Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r8.anchor: Others take clear proof as a reference to the Prophet Muhammad

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r9.claim: The proof can mean revelation, books, and prophets sent to every community, since the Quran uses this expression for many prophets and their scriptures.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r9.anchor: a reference to the phenomena of revelation and thus to the books and prophets sent to all communities

STUDYQURAN:98:1/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r10.claim: On this reading, the People of the Book are those said to have altered scriptures sent through earlier prophets.
STUDYQURAN:98:1/r10.anchor: those who are said to have altered the scriptures that had been sent to them through previous prophets

TAB:98:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:98:1/r1.claim: Mujahid says the disbelievers would not desist until the truth became clear to them.
TAB:98:1/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  لم يكونوا ليَنتهوا حتى يتبين لهم الحقّ

TAB:98:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:1/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses mufakkīn as people ending or desisting from their present condition.
TAB:98:1/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  منتهين عما هم فيه

TAB:98:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:1/r3.claim: Qatadah identifies the awaited clear proof as this Qur’an.
TAB:98:1/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله {  مُنْفَكّينَ حَتَى تأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيّنَةُ } :  أي هذا القرآن

TAB:98:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:98:1/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they would not cease until that separating proof came.
TAB:98:1/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله :  {  وَالمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  لم يكونوا منتهين حتى يأتيهم ذلك المنفَكّ

TAB:98:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB:98:1/r5.claim: Another view says the People of the Book retained Muhammad’s description in their scriptures until he was sent, then split over him.
TAB:98:1/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون :  بل معنى ذلك أن أهل الكتاب وهم المشركون ،   لم يكونوا تاركين صفة محمد في كتابهم ،   حتى بُعث

TAB:98:1/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r6.speaker: author
TAB:98:1/r6.claim: The author prefers that the disbelievers were not divided over Muhammad until the proof came: God’s sending him as a messenger to creation.
TAB:98:1/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة أن يقال :  معنى ذلك :  لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين مفترقين في أمر محمد

TAB:98:1/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r7.speaker: author
TAB:98:1/r7.claim: Here mufakkīn means separation of two things, so the verb can stand without a complement; if it meant ‘continued to be,’ it would need one.
TAB:98:1/r7.anchor: وقوله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } في هذا الموضع عندي من انفكاك الشيئين أحدهما من الآخر ،   ولذلك صَلُح بغير خبر ،   ولو كان بمعنى ما زال ،   احتاج إلى خبر

TAB:98:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r8.speaker: author
TAB:98:1/r8.claim: He resumes with the indefinite ‘a messenger from God’ to explain the definite proof, by analogy with the wording in 85:15–16.
TAB:98:1/r8.anchor: واستؤنف قوله {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ } وهي نكرة على البيّنة ،   وهي معرفة ،   كما قيل :  {  ذُو الْعَرْشِ المَجِيدُ فَعّالٌ

TAB:98:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:98:3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the disbelievers would not desist until the truth became clear to them.
TAB:98:3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  لم يكونوا ليَنتهوا حتى يتبين لهم الحقّ

TAB:98:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:3/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses mufakkīn as people ending or desisting from their present condition.
TAB:98:3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  منتهين عما هم فيه

TAB:98:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:98:3/r3.claim: Qatadah identifies the awaited clear proof as this Qur’an.
TAB:98:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله {  مُنْفَكّينَ حَتَى تأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيّنَةُ } :  أي هذا القرآن

TAB:98:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:98:3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they would not cease until that separating proof came.
TAB:98:3/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله :  {  وَالمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكّينَ } قال :  لم يكونوا منتهين حتى يأتيهم ذلك المنفَكّ

TAB:98:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB:98:3/r5.claim: Another view says the People of the Book retained Muhammad’s description in their scriptures until he was sent, then split over him.
TAB:98:3/r5.anchor:
لم يكونوا منتهين حتى يأتيهم ذلك المنفَكّ .
وقال آخرون :  بل معنى ذلك أن أهل الكتاب وهم

TAB:98:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r6.speaker: author
TAB:98:3/r6.claim: The author prefers that the disbelievers were not divided over Muhammad until the proof came: God’s sending him as a messenger to creation.
TAB:98:3/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة أن يقال :  معنى ذلك :  لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين مفترقين في أمر محمد

TAB:98:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r7.speaker: author
TAB:98:3/r7.claim: Here mufakkīn means separation of two things, so the verb can stand without a complement; if it meant ‘continued to be,’ it would need one.
TAB:98:3/r7.anchor: وقوله :  {  مُنْفَكّينَ } في هذا الموضع عندي من انفكاك الشيئين أحدهما من الآخر ،   ولذلك صَلُح بغير خبر ،   ولو كان بمعنى ما زال ،   احتاج إلى خبر

TAB:98:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r8.speaker: author
TAB:98:3/r8.claim: He resumes with the indefinite ‘a messenger from God’ to explain the definite proof, by analogy with the wording in 85:15–16.
TAB:98:3/r8.anchor: واستؤنف قوله {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ } وهي نكرة على البيّنة ،   وهي معرفة ،   كما قيل :  {  ذُو الْعَرْشِ المَجِيدُ فَعّالٌ

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the unbelievers’ being unseparated as their not ending their state until the truth became clear.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {منفكين} [البينة: 1] قال: «لم يكونوا لينتهوا حتى يتبين لهم الحق»

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains the term as ceasing from their present state and says the proof is this Qur’an.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، في قوله {منفكين} [البينة: 1] قال: منتهين عما هم فيه

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says they would not cease until the proof came.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله: {والمشركين منفكين} [البينة: 1] قال: «لم يكونوا منتهين حتى يأتيهم؛ ذلك المنفك»

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r4.claim: Another view says the People of Scripture retained Muhammad’s description in their books until he was sent, then split over him.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك أن أهل الكتاب وهم المشركون، لم يكونوا تاركين صفة محمد في كتابهم، حتى بعث

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that unbelievers were not divided over Muhammad until God sent him as Messenger; afterward some denied and some believed, though before his mission they agreed he was a prophet.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r5.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصحة أن يقال: معنى ذلك: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين مفترقين في أمر محمد

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r6.claim: Here unseparated derives from two things separating from one another; on that reading the verb needs no predicate, unlike the sense “never ceased.”
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r6.anchor: وقوله {منفكين} [البينة: 1] في هذا الموضع عندي من انفكاك الشيئين أحدهما من الآخر، ولذلك صلح بغير خبر

TABATABAI:98:1/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1/r3.claim: The Prophet is the clear proof required by divine guidance; those who disbelieved in his Islamic call among the People of the Book and polytheists could not be left without it.
TABATABAI:98:1/r3.anchor: أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من مصاديق الحجة البينة القائمة على الناس

TABATABAI:98:1/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1/r4.claim: ‘Those who disbelieved’ means those who rejected the Islamic prophetic call; min is partitive, and the polytheists are non-scriptural idolaters and others.
TABATABAI:98:1/r4.anchor: الكافرون بالدعوة النبوية الإسلامية من أهل الكتاب والمشركين

TABATABAI:98:1/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1/r5.claim: Munfakkīn means separating from a close attachment; here they remained bound to the demands of guidance until the proof arrived and then were left to themselves.
TABATABAI:98:1/r5.anchor: من الانفكاك وهو الانفصال عن شدة اتصال

TABATABAI:98:1/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1/r6.claim: God does not mislead a people after guiding them until He clarifies what they must avoid.
TABATABAI:98:1/r6.anchor: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون

TABATABAI:98:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r1.claim: Bayyina means an evident proof; the verse’s future wording says unbelievers would remain attached to their stance until Muhammad came, who is himself the proof.
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r1.anchor: والبينة هي الحجة الظاهرة والمعنى لم يكن الذين كفروا برسالة النبي

TABATABAI:98:7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:7/r3.speaker: أبو الجارود
TABATABAI:98:7/r3.claim: Abu al-Jarud transmits Imam al-Baqir’s identification of the clear proof as Muhammad, the Messenger of God.
TABATABAI:98:7/r3.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال البينة محمد رسول الله

TABRISI:98:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:1/r3.claim: Infikak means separation after strong attachment and is used mostly with negation, as in a line by Dhu al-Rumma about camels that only stop to kneel or be driven to a remote land.
TABRISI:98:1/r3.anchor: قلائص ما تنفك إلا مناخة على الخسف أو نرمي بها بلدا قفرا

TABRISI:98:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:1/r4.claim: Bayyina is a clear proof distinguishing truth from falsehood; its root carries the sense of separation. The Prophet, fair testimony, and every proof are called bayyina.
TABRISI:98:1/r4.anchor: والبينة الحجة الظاهرة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل وأصلها من البينونة

TABRISI:98:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:1/r8.claim: The verse addresses Jews, Christians, and idol-worshipping polytheists from Arabs and others; munfakkin can mean separating or stopping from disbelief and worship of others, an interpretation attributed to Ibn Abbas through Ata and al-Kalbi.
TABRISI:98:1/r8.anchor: ومن المشركين الذين هم عبدة الأوثان من العرب وغيرهم

TABRISI:98:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:1/r9.claim: The future-tense phrase until the proof came refers to the past, as in the statement about what demons recited in 2:102.

TABRISI:98:1-4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1-4/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:98:1-4/r2.claim: Alternatively, they could not leave unbelief until God's proof came and established the argument against them.
TABRISI:98:1-4/r2.anchor: لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين من حجج الله حتى تأتيهم البينة التي تقوم بها الحجة عليهم

THALABI:v10p260#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r1.claim: The People of the Book here are Jews and Christians, and the polytheists are idol worshippers; they had not ceased their disbelief and associationism until the clear proof came.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r1.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى، والمشركون وهم عبدة الأوثان، منفكين منتهين عن كفرهم وشركهم،

THALABI:v10p260#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r2.claim: Philologists explain munfakkīn as ceasing or disappearing; Arabic usage ma انفكّ فلان يفعل means someone continued doing something, from the root sense of opening or releasing.
