THALABI:v10p260#2/r2.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: زائلين، يقول: العرب: ما انفك فلان يفعل كذا، أي ما زال،

THALABI:v10p260#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r3.speaker: طرفة
THALABI:v10p260#2/r3.claim: His verse illustrates the Arabic expression for something that does not cease.

THALABI:v10p260#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r4.claim: The clear proof is Muhammad, who brought the Qur'an, exposed their error and ignorance, and guided them to faith.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r4.anchor: حتى تأتيهم البينة الحجة الواضحة وهي محمد

THALABI:v10p260#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p260#2/r5.claim: He interprets the verse as saying they would not abandon their prior description of Muhammad until his mission; after his coming, they split over him.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان معناه لم يكن هؤلاء الكفار تاركين صفة محمد

THALABI:v10p260#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r6.claim: Rasūlun min Allāh explains al-bayyina by apposition, an indefinite noun replacing a definite one, as in 85:15–16.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r6.anchor: ثم فسر البينة فقال: رسول من الله. فأبدل النكرة من المعرفة كقوله: ذو العرش المجيد فعال لما يريد

THALABI:v10p260#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r7.claim: Yatlū means reads, and ṣuḥuf means books purified of falsehood.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r7.anchor: يتلوا يقرأ صحفا كتبا مطهرة من الباطل

THALABI:v10p260#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r8.claim: The books contain God's upright, just rulings.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r8.anchor: فيها كتب من الله قيمة مستقيمة عادلة

THALABI:v10p260#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p260#2/r9.claim: The People of the Book divided over Muhammad and denied him only after the proof in their scriptures that he was a sent prophet.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r9.anchor: فكذبوه إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة البيان في كتبهم

THALABI:v10p260#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r10.speaker: قال العلماء
THALABI:v10p260#2/r10.claim: They assign the opening clause to those among the People of the Book and polytheists who believed, and the clause about division to People of the Book who remained unbelievers after the proofs were established.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r10.anchor: قال العلماء: من أول السورة إلى قوله: فيها كتب قيمة حكمها في من آمن

THALABI:v10p260#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p260#2/r11.speaker: بعض أئمة أهل اللغة
THALABI:v10p260#2/r11.claim: Another lexical interpretation derives munfakkīn from a phrase for a woman's pelvic separation at childbirth and collapse; the verse then means they were not to be punished until proof came through a messenger and revealed books.
THALABI:v10p260#2/r11.anchor: قوله: منفكين أي هالكين من قوله انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

THALABI:v10p261/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r1.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v10p261/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads wa-l-mushrikūn in the nominative; the source also records variants in the codices of Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy, including an accusative rasūlan.
THALABI:v10p261/r1.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش (والمشركون) رفعا، وفي مصحف عبد الله (لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين)

THALABI:v10p261/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r2.speaker: أبي
THALABI:v10p261/r2.claim: Ubayy's reading has mā kāna and rasūlan in the accusative as a detached circumstantial expression.
THALABI:v10p261/r2.anchor: وفي حرف أبي (ما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة رسولا من الله) بالنصب

THALABI:v10p261/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p261/r3.claim: The disbelievers were commanded only to worship God sincerely in tawḥīd and obedience, turning from all religions toward Islam.
THALABI:v10p261/r3.anchor: وما أمروا يعني هؤلاء الكفار إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين يعني إلا أن يعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين التوحيد والطاعة

THALABI:v10p261/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p261/r4.claim: He glosses ḥunafāʾ as people performing pilgrimage.
THALABI:v10p261/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: حجاجا، وقال قتادة:

THALABI:v10p261/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p261/r5.claim: He defines ḥanīfiyya through circumcision, prohibiting marriage to close female relatives, and performing the rites.
THALABI:v10p261/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحنيفية هي الختان وتحريم الأمهات والبنات والأخوات والعمات والخالات، وإقامة المناسك.

THALABI:v10p261/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r6.speaker: سعيد بن حمزة
THALABI:v10p261/r6.claim: He says Arabs call someone a ḥanīf only if he performs pilgrimage, is circumcised, and observes the rites.
THALABI:v10p261/r6.anchor: وقال سعيد بن حمزة: لا تسمي العرب حنيفا إلا من حج واختتن

THALABI:v10p261/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p261/r7.claim: Prayer and almsgiving are the upright religion; qayyima is feminine because it refers back to the religious community or law, or its feminine ending intensifies the sense.
THALABI:v10p261/r7.anchor: دين القيمة المستقيمة فأضاف الدين إلى القيمة

THALABI:v10p261/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r8.speaker: أبو سهل محمد بن محمد بن الأشعث الطالقاني
THALABI:v10p261/r8.claim: He takes al-qayyima to mean the previously mentioned books, with the religion attributed to those books as what they enjoin; he compares 2:213.
THALABI:v10p261/r8.anchor: إن القيمة هاهنا الكتب التي جرى ذكرها، والدين مضاف إليها على معنى: وذلك دين الكتب القيمة

THALABI:v10p261/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r9.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v10p261/r9.claim: Reporting al-Khalīl, he explains qayyima as the plural of qayyim or qāʾim: the religion of those who uphold tawḥīd.
THALABI:v10p261/r9.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سألت الخليل بن أحمد عن قوله سبحانه: وذلك دين القيمة فقال: القيمة جمع القيم،

THALABI:v10p261/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p261/r10.claim: The unbelievers are the worst creatures; Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read al-bariʾa with hamza on the original form, while other readers omit the hamza and double the consonant.
THALABI:v10p261/r10.anchor: قرأ نافع البرئة بالهمزة في الحرفين ومثله روى ابن ذكوان عن أهل الشام

THALABI:v10p261/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p261/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p261/r11.claim: One explanation of the unhamzated reading is that it dropped the hamza and substituted a consonant resembling it.
THALABI:v10p261/r11.anchor: أحدهما أنه ترك الهمزة وأدخل الشبه به عوضا منه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r1.claim: “Those who disbelieved from the People of the Book” means Jews and Christians, while “the polytheists” means Arab idolaters; the two groups differ in their relation to scripture and beliefs such as calling ʿUzayr or the Messiah God's son.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r1.anchor: {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب} يعني اليهود والنصارى. {والمشركين}. يعني مشركي العرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r2.claim: Munfakkīn means departing or ceasing; al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad give the same gloss, supported by poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: {منفكين}. قال أبو عبيدة (¬3)، والأخفش (¬4)، والمبرد (¬5): زائلين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads Dhū al-Rumma's “lā tanfakku” as separation, since “never ceases except halted” does not fit the sense “continues”; other grammarians take it as “continues” with lā inserted for poetic necessity or emphasis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r3.anchor: فأما قول ذي الرمة: لا ينفك إلا مناخة. فجعله الفراء من الانفكاك الذي هو الانفصال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r4.speaker: طرفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r4.claim: Ṭarafa's line “lā yanfakku” demonstrates the sense “continues,” as opposed to physical separation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p203#2/r4.anchor: ومن هذا قول طرفة: فآليت (¬2) لا ينفك كشحي بطانة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r1.claim: In this verse munfakkīn means separating or ceasing from their unbelief, not “continuing”; ʿAṭāʾ, al-Kalbī from Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Muqātil say they had not abandoned disbelief and worship of other gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r1.anchor: وأما الذي في الآية فهو من الانفصال، وليس بمعنى: لم يزالوا (¬1). قال عطاء (¬2)، والكلبي (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r2.speaker: ابن عرفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r2.claim: The phrase “until the clear proof comes to them” has past meaning even though its form is present tense, as with 2:102.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: {حتى تأتيهم البينة} قال ابن عرفة: أي حتى أتتهم (¬7)، لفظه لفظ المضارع، ومعناه الماضي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.claim: The clear proof is Muḥammad; Muqātil says he explained their error and polytheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r3.anchor: وقوله: {البينة} هو قال ابن عبا لهم س: يريد محمدا -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.claim: Bayyina is manifest evidence distinguishing truth from falsehood; the Prophet, a just witness, or any proof may be called bayyina.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r4.anchor: ومعنى {البينة}: الحجة الظاهرة التي يتميز بها الحق من الباطل، # فالنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- بينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.claim: The disbelievers had not left unbelief and polytheism until Muḥammad came with the Qurʾān, exposed their error, and called them to faith; this describes God's favor and concerns those from both groups who believed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: إخبار الله تعالى عن الكفار أنهم لم (¬3) ينتهوا عن كفرهم وشركهم بالله حتى أتاهم محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.claim: “A messenger from God” is an appositive explaining the definite “clear proof.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: رسول: رفع على البدل من البينة، والتفسير لها (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the indefinite “messenger” as a fresh nominative rather than an appositive to the definite “clear proof.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p207/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء: "رسول" نكرة استؤنف على البينة، وهي معرفة كما قال:

WAHIDI-QT:98:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:98:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:98:1/r1.claim: People of the Book means Jews and Christians; the polytheists are Arab disbelievers, who continued in unbelief until Muhammad and the Quran brought proof and clarity; the passage concerns those among both groups who believed.
WAHIDI-QT:98:1/r1.anchor: منتهين زائلين عن كفرهم { حتى تأتيهم البينة } يعني أتتهم البينة ،   أي البيان والبصيرة ،   وهو محمد عليه السلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r1.claim: The disbelieving People of the Book are Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are the unbelieving Arabs.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r1.anchor: من أهل الكتاب } أي: اليهود والنصارى { والمشركين } يعني: كفار العرب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r2.claim: ‘Breaking away’ means ceasing and departing from disbelief; the clear proof is Muhammad and the Qur'an, who came to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r2.anchor: منتهين زائلين عن كفرهم { حتى تأتيهم البينة } يعني: أتتهم البينة، أي: البيان والبصيرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r3.claim: They did not leave unbelief until Muhammad was sent; this refers to those from both groups who believed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r3.anchor: يقول: لم يتركوا كفرهم حتى بعث إليهم محمد عليه السلام، وهذا فيمن آمن من الفريقين،

ASAD-NOTES:98:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:intro/r1.speaker: some authorities
ASAD-NOTES:98:intro/r1.claim: Some authorities classify the surah as Medinan, while many others regard it as a late Meccan revelation; its title word occurs at the end of verse 1.
ASAD-NOTES:98:intro/r1.anchor: many others regard it as a late Meccan revelation.

ASAD-NOTES:98:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:98:1/r1.claim: Asad renders the verse to mean that deniers among scriptural communities and polytheists are not condemned before the full evidence of truth reaches them.
ASAD-NOTES:98:1/r1.anchor: should ever be abandoned [by Him] ere there comes unto them the [full] evidence of the truth

ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n1/r1.claim: The polytheists named here include idol-worshippers and animists who have no revealed scripture to rely upon.
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n1/r1.anchor: idol-worshippers or animists (in the anthropological sense of this word) who have never had any revealed scripture to fall back upon

ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r2.claim: Asad rejects the common reading that the deniers only separated from error when Muhammad and the Qur’an arrived: not all accepted them, and verse 4 says scriptural communities broke unity after the evidence came.
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r2.anchor: This assumption is, however, deficient on two counts: firstly, it is well-known that not all of the erring ones

ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r3.speaker: Ibn Taymiyyah
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r3.claim: Following Ibn Taymiyyah, Asad reads munfakkin as “not abandoned” or condemned by God until people have been shown the right, including through earlier prophets and revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r3.anchor: Ibn Taymiyyah (see Tafsir Sitt Suwar, pp. 391 ff.); and it is his interpretation that I have followed

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r1.claim: Min can be partitive or explanatory, attached to an omitted phrase and describing the disbelievers; the syntax permits several ways of dividing the two groups.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r1.anchor: “min” teb‘îziye veya beyâniye, mahzûfa müte‘allik olup كائنين من أهل الكتاب والمشركين yahut الكائنون من أهل الكتاب والمشركين takdîrinde zarf-ı müstekar

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r2.claim: The wording can mean some disbelievers from each group, disbelievers as two groups, or disbelievers who belong to both the People of the Book and the polytheists.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r2.anchor: Bu iki kısımdan kâfirler veya iki kısım kâfirler ki bazısı ehl-i kitab bazısı müşrik, yahut hem ehl-i kitabdan hem de müşriklerden olan kâfirler demek olabilir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.claim: The reading that includes People of the Book who also held explicit or implicit shirk best fits verse 3, which names only them.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.anchor: Üçüncü âyette yalnız ehl-i kitab zikrolunmasına bu mâna daha akrebdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r4.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; naming them this way suggests their rejection of Muhammad and the Qur’an also amounts to rejecting their own Torah and Gospel.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r4.anchor: Ehl-i kitab Yehûd ve Nasârâdır. Burada “ehl-i kitab” unvânıyla ifade edilmeleri bunlar içinden Allah’a küfredenlerin küfürleri

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r5.claim: Polytheists include all who assign divinity to anything besides Allah, broader than idol worshippers; it includes polytheists and those making their desires gods.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r5.anchor: Müşrikler, Allah tealâ’ya esnâmdan veya gayrısından her ne suretle olursa olsun şirk itikad edenler, yani Allah’tan başkasına ulûhiyet isnad eyleyenlerdir ki putperestlerden e‘amdır

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r6.claim: Since Allah alone is truly worthy of worship, assigning worship to another independently or in partnership is shirk; multiplicity of attributes with unity of essence is not.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r6.anchor: Vahdet-i zât ile beraber sıfâtın kesreti şirki iktizâ etmez. Şirk ancak zât-ı ilâhda küllî veya cüz’î kesret itikadındadır

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r7.claim: The Trinity is shirk and self-contradictory because it claims both plurality and unity of divine essence.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r7.anchor: teslis tevhîdi hakikatte tevhid değil, zatın hem ta‘addüdü hem ittihâdı davasını tazammun ettiği için hem şirk hem tenakuzdur

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r8.claim: Lam makes the category general, so polytheists include all kinds; some instead restrict the term to the familiar Arab idolaters of Mecca and Medina.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r8.anchor: Burada لَمْ cins için olarak وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ gerek putperest ve gerek sâire ale’lumûm müşriklere şâmildir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r9.claim: He rejects restricting the phrase to known Arab idolaters, since the prior definite phrase already identifies the known disbelievers as some within both broader groups.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r9.anchor: ahd mânası daha evvel ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟’da mülâhaza edilmek kâfîdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r10.claim: Munfakkin is the predicate of lam yakun, and hatta attaches to it: the disbelievers would not leave their condition before the clear proof came.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r10.anchor: “Münfekkîn” لَمْ يَكُنِ’ün haberidir. حَتَّىٰ da ona müte‘alliktir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r11.claim: Bayyina denotes an evident proof that makes another matter clear, such as a witness, articulate proof, or miracle; here it is a decisive proof establishing truth.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r11.anchor: Burada da hakkı beyan ve isbat edecek açık ve kat‘î hüccet-i nâtıka veya mu‘cize demektir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.claim: The bayyina is the Messenger from God, either by apposition or as an explanation of bayyina through an omitted subject and predicate.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r12.anchor: Allah tarafından risaletle gönderilmiş bir peygamber gelinceye kadar infikâk edecek değillerdi

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.claim: Before a messenger, people could not fully know or unite upon true monotheism and could be excused; after the proof came, the People of the Book had no excuse for persisting in disbelief.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.anchor: öyle bir beyyine gelmedikçe tamamen hak ve tevhid dinini bilip de birleşecek ve hâllerini değiştirecek bir vaziyette bulunmuyorlardı ve bunda mâzur olabilirlerdi

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r1.speaker: Vâhidî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r1.claim: Razi reports Wahidi’s statement that this verse is among the Qur’an’s hardest in wording and exegesis, though Wahidi did not summarize the difficulty.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r1.anchor: Vâhidî Kitâbü’l- Basît’te: “Bu âyet Kur’an’daki âyetlerin gerek nazım ve gerek tefsir itibariyle en zorudur

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.claim: Razi frames the puzzle: if munfakkin means leaving disbelief and hatta marks an endpoint, the first verse implies conversion after the Messenger, while verse 4 says division followed the proof.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.anchor: Sonra infikâkleri ne şeyden, Allah teâlâ onu zikretmemiştir. Lâkin murad, bulundukları küfür hâlinden demek olduğu mâlumdur

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.claim: The preferred Keşşaf solution reads verse 1 as the disbelievers’ earlier pledge to stay in their religions until the promised Prophet Muhammad came; verse 4 reports their failure to keep that pledge.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.anchor: Birincisi ve en güzeli Sâhib-Keşşâf’ın telhis ettiği vecihtir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.claim: On that reading, they promised to unite in truth when the Prophet came but instead split and persisted in disbelief; Razi illustrates this with a sinner who increases sin after becoming rich.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.anchor: onlar o Peygamber geldiği zaman hak üzerinde ittifak ile bir kelimede toplanmak vaad ediyorlardı, sonra da haktan asıl ayrılmaları ve küfürde kararları o Resul gelince oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r5.speaker: Kādî Abdülcebbar
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r5.claim: Qadi Abd al-Jabbar reads the verse as saying the disbelievers would not leave disbelief even after the proof arrived, but the author notes that hatta does not have this sense in Arabic.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r5.anchor: Kādî Abdülcebbar böyle demiş, lâkin lügatta حَتَّىٰ’nın bu mânası olmadığı söylenmiştir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.claim: A third proposal makes munfakkin refer to mentioning the coming Messenger’s virtues: they spoke of his merits before his arrival, then disagreed after he came.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.anchor: Üçüncüsü: Münfekkîn küfürden infikâke değil, beyyine olarak gelecek resûlün menâkıb ve fezâilini anmaktan[^12] infikâk etmedikleri mânasına olmalıdır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.claim: A fourth proposal says that, after the Messenger came, the whole group no longer remained disbelieving because some believed and some did not, satisfying hatta’s implication of change.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.anchor: Çünkü mecmû‘u o küfürde kalmadılar, bazısı mü’min bazısı da kâfir oldular. Bu kadarı da ‘hattâ’nın medlûlüyle amele kâfîdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.claim: A fifth proposal says the Prophet’s mission shook their prior certainty in inherited religions; some converted, while others divided through stubbornness despite recognizing their old religions’ weakness.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.anchor: Resûlullah ba‘s olununca alışmış yapışmış oldukları eski dinleri hakkındaki cezm ü itikadları mütezelzil ve evvelki fikr ü kanaatleri perişan oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.claim: This proposal distinguishes infikak as detachment from something once clung to from tafarruq as dispersion, showing how the post-Prophet condition differed from the prior one.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.anchor: bir şeyin bir şeyden infikâki ona yapışmış iken kopup ayrılması demektir. Tefrika da dağılmaktır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.claim: Razi transmits these five solutions but identifies the first as preferred; the author finds Keşşaf’s wording more subtle and compatible with several proposals.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.anchor: Râzî bu beş vechi hikâye ve beyan etmiş olmakla beraber kavl-i muhtâr birinci vecih olduğunu da ihtar eylemiştir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud and others follow the first solution but supply the prior state as the object: their pledge and resolve to believe and follow the last Messenger.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.anchor: Ebussuud ve daha birçokları da Keşşâf’ın birinci vechi üzerinde yürümekle beraber “infikâk”in müte‘allakını mukaddemâ üzerinde bulundukları şey

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.claim: The account says the People of the Book prayed for victory through the last Prophet and threatened Arab opponents that they would defeat them with him; later polytheists may have adopted the claim.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.anchor: Ehl-i kitabdan bu vaadin vukū‘unda şüphe yoktur. Hatta onlar onunla Allah’tan fütûhât diliyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.claim: They asked the People of the Book whether Muhammad was the figure named in their scripture, yet after his arrival the People of the Book disbelieved and divided.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.anchor: Resûlullah hakkında gidip ehl-i kitaba soruyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.claim: The author finds his earlier explanation most apparent: before the decisive proof, people were in a state where they could not leave their inherited condition; after it, the People of the Book should have believed.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.anchor: bunu bu esas üzere, yani bulundukları hâlden infikâk mânasına olarak bâlâda îzah ettiğimiz diğer bir vech ile anlamak

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.claim: The pledge reading is awkward when extended to polytheists; reading the object as their religions or disbelief would imply they should depart from them, though the proof was sent for that purpose.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.anchor: Ancak bunu o vaad ve azm ile tefsir etmek Sûre-i Bakara âyetine muvâfık olsa da müşriklere teşmîli itibariyle biraz dolambaçlı geliyor

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.claim: Before Muhammad’s mission was a period of interruption when religions were corrupted, pagans and non-pagans mixed, and truth and falsehood could not be distinguished.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden önceki zaman dinlerin tahrif ve teşvîşe uğradığı müşrikle gayr-i müşrikin karıştığı

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.claim: Given the rule that punishment does not come before a messenger, the interval is an excuse period without responsibility; before decisive proof, the default is to leave people in their existing state.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.anchor: Fetret zamanları ise وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا hükmüne[^22] nazaran mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmeyen bir mazeret zamanı demektir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.claim: Prophets are sent to illuminate truth and duty during such periods, distinguishing believers and disbelievers so accountability can apply.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.anchor: Ve beşeriyetin böyle hakk u bâtılı seçemeyecek bir fetret ve zulmet içinde kaldığı zamanlardır ki taraf-ı ilâhîden

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.claim: Following the previous surah’s account of revelation’s wisdom, this surah explains the pre-Prophetic interval: before Qur’an and Messenger the disbelievers could be excused, but after proof, especially the People of the Book’s rejection and division, they deserved punishment.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.anchor: Kur’ân’ın inzâliyle beyyine-i ilâhiye olan Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden evvel ehl-i kitabdan ve müşriklerden bulunan kâfirler bulundukları hâllerinden ayrılmamakta mâzur olsalar da, hak dini beyan eden bu beyyine geldikten sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r1.claim: The People of the Book here especially means Jews and Christians around Medina, and polytheists means the pagan Arabs; though local groups are named, the ruling concerns all humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r1.anchor: yahudilerle hıristiyanlar; “müşrikler”den maksat ise dönemin putperest Araplar’ıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r2.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r2.claim: Most exegetes say Jews, Christians, and pagans would not abandon disbelief until a clear proof, namely a prophet, came to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r2.anchor: kendilerine açık kanıt yani peygamber gelinceye kadar içinde bulundukları inkârcılıktan ayrılıp ona son vermeyeceklerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r3.speaker: Diğer bir yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r3.claim: Another reading says God would not let the People of the Book and polytheists addressed by Muhammad die before sending them a new divine message at the appointed time.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r3.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in muhatapları olan Ehl-i kitap ile müşrikleri, –yeni bir ilâhî mesajın zamanı geldiği için– o mesajı göndermeden dünyadan ayırmayacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r4.speaker: Üçüncü yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r4.claim: A third reading says these groups would not be punished until messenger and proof had been sent to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r4.anchor: kendilerine elçi ve kanıt gelmedikçe, gönderilmedikçe cezalandırılmayacakları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r5.claim: The author finds the third reading more contextually fitting: despite human capacities to distinguish right from wrong, divine mercy means those not reached by clear proof and the message are not punished, as stated at 17:15.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r5.anchor: açık kanıt göndermediği ve mesajının ulaşmadığı kimseleri yaptıklarından dolayı cezalandırmayacağını

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.claim: Al-Bayyinah complements al-Qadr: the Qur’an’s exaltedness is explained, and the People of the Book and Makkan idolaters rejected it from conceit, not genuine doubt, using demands for a sign as a pretext.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.anchor: conceit and arrogance which led them to this attitude

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r2.claim: Even if the opponents witnessed the greatest signs and miracles, they would invent excuses to conceal their haughtiness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r2.anchor: would not convince them in this matter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r1.claim: The Jews initially held back from active opposition because they expected Quraysh to end the new faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r1.anchor: they did not take any practical part in opposing this call

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r2.claim: When Jews began supporting Quraysh, they supplied objections and questions for them to ask the Prophet in order to pester and harass him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r2.anchor: they were told to ask the Prophet (sws) in order to pester

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r3.claim: At first the Jews expected Quraysh opposition to end Islam; when it spread, they supplied objections and invented tests, including a heavenly fire consuming a prophet’s sacrifice, to help Quraysh challenge Muhammad.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r3.anchor: any prophethood unless a fire descends from the sky

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r4.claim: The discourse assures the Prophet that Quraysh and the People of the Book will not desist or accept the Qur’an; they would believe only if an angel descended reciting scripture.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p400/r4.anchor: They will only believe when an angel will descend from the skies whilst reading some scripture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r1.claim: Lam yakun is treated as a complete verb rather than an incomplete verb, like the usage in 4:17; the translation follows this grammatical reading.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r1.anchor: The translation of the verse has been done

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r2.claim: The omitted object of ‘denied’ is the Qur’an and the Messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r2.anchor: The suppressed object is the Qur’ ān and the Messenger which they denied

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r3.claim: The People of the Book and idolaters are the two leading opposition groups; Qur’anic mushrikūn here is a proper noun for Quraysh or the Ishmaelites.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r4.claim: Min is partitive: the verse targets only the hostile subset, since both groups included Muslims, impartial people, and balanced non-Muslims whom the Qur’an praised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r4.anchor: referred to here who were not willing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r5.claim: Bayyinah means a manifest sign, specifically an undeniable miracle demanded by stubborn opponents, a demand the Qur’an mentions elsewhere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p402/r5.anchor: By such a manifest sign they meant that such a miracle be shown to them which they would not be able to deny

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r1.claim: The People of the Book demanded a heavenly book and had earlier demanded that Moses show them God; the idolaters likewise wanted individual open pages, as cited in 4:153 and 74:52.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r1.anchor: The People of the Book ask you to bring down directly for them a book from the heavens

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r2.claim: These opponents reject revelation to one person and demand a separate scripture for each of them before accepting that God revealed guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r2.anchor: their demand is that for each of them a separate scripture be revealed

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p387/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p387/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p387/r1.claim: Qatāda explains munfakkīn as coming to an end or ceasing from their present state.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p387/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ منفكين ﴾ قال منتهين عما هم فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r3.claim: After the preceding sūra's mention of Qur'anic revelation, this passage says disbelievers persisted in their state until the Messenger came reciting the purified pages he was commanded to read.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r3.anchor: ذكر هنا أن الكفار لم يكونوا منفكين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r4.claim: The verse divides the disbelievers into People of Scripture and polytheists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r4.anchor: وقسم الكافرين هنا إلى أهل كتاب وأهل إشراك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r5.claim: Some readers raise al-mushrikūn, coordinating it with all those who disbelieve.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p517/r5.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء: والمشركون رفعا عطفا على الذين كفروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r1.claim: Most readers place al-mushrikīn in the genitive, coordinating it with People of Scripture; these are Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are Arab idolaters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r1.anchor: والجمهور: بالجر عطفا على أهل الكتاب، وأهل الكتاب اليهود والنصارى، والمشركون عبدة الأوثان من العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the People of Scripture as the Jews of Medina—Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr, and Banū Qaynuqāʿ—and the polytheists as those around Mecca and Medina.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أهل الكتاب اليهود الذين كانوا بيثرب هم قريظة والنضير وبنو قينقاع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r3.claim: Mujāhid and others say the two groups did not leave disbelief and error until the clear proof came.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: لم يكونوا منفكين عن الكفر والضلال حتى جاءتهم البينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r4.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others say they continued to recognize Muhammad's true prophethood and expect him until the clear proof came, after which they split.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء وغيره: لم يكونوا منفكين عن معرفة صحة نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والتوكف لأمره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says both groups had claimed before the mission that they would not abandon their religions until the promised prophet described in Torah and Gospel arrived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كان الكفار من الفريقين يقولون قبل المبعث: لا ننفك مما نحن فيه من ديننا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers a third reading: none could escape God's power and care until He sent a warner to establish proof, complete blessing for believers, and prevent people being left aimless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويتجه في معنى الآية قول ثالث بارع المعنى، وذلك أنه يكون المراد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r7.claim: Another interpretation says they would not die until the proof came.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r7.anchor: وقيل: لم يكونوا منفكين عن حياتهم فيموتوا حتى تأتيهم البينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r8.claim: The apparent meaning is that the groups remained joined in mutual approval: each accepted the other's chosen scripture or idols, and their friendship and unity lasted until the proof arrived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن المعنى: لم يكونوا منفكين، أي منفصلا بعضهم من بعض، بل كان كل منهم مقرا الآخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r9.claim: Another view derives munfakkīn as perishing or coming apart: they would not be punished or destroyed until messengers and books established proof.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r9.anchor: وقيل: معنى منفكين: هالكين، من قولهم: انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r10.claim: The author parses munfakkīn as an active participle from the complete verb infakka, not the incomplete kāna-like verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r10.anchor: ومنفكين اسم فاعل من انفك، وهي التامة وليست الداخلة على المبتدأ والخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r11.claim: The author rejects grammarians' incomplete-verb analysis because it requires an omitted predicate, which his school says cannot be dropped from kāna and its sisters except by poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p518/r11.anchor: وقال بعض النحاة: هي الناقصة، ويقدر منفكين: عارفين أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r1.claim: Al-bayyina means a clear, manifest proof.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r1.claim: The sura is also called al-Qiyama, al-Balad, al-Munfakkin, al-Bariyya, and Lam Yakun, as al-Bahr notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة القيامة وسورة البلد وسورة المنفكين وسورة البرية وسورة لم يكن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r2.claim: Reports disagree about whether it is Meccan or Medinan: al-Bahr gives the majority as Meccan, while Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAta ibn Yasar call it Medinan, as does al-Tahrir, which also calls that the majority view.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r2.anchor: قال في البحر مكية في قول الجمهور وقال ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار مدنية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r3.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is Meccan, a choice also made by Yahya ibn Sallam; Ibn al-Faras says Meccan is more likely and relates that view from ʿAisha.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r3.anchor: وروي أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنها مكية واختاره يحيى بن سلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir decisively regards it as Medinan, citing a report about its revelation and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r4.anchor: وجزم ابن كثير بأنها مدنية واستدل على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r5.speaker: أبو خيثمة البدري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r5.claim: Abu Khaythama al-Badri reports that Gabriel commanded the Prophet to recite the newly revealed sura to Ubayy; Ubayy wept when told he had been named. Al-Alusi calls this the sounder view.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r5.anchor: لما نزلت لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب إلى آخرها قال جبريل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r6.claim: The Basran count gives the sura nine verses, while other regional counts give eight.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r6.anchor: وآيها تسع في البصري وثمان في غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r7.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي حكيم عن مطر المزني أو المدني
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r7.claim: A report on its merit says God addresses the one who recites “Lam yakun,” promising to grant Paradise until the servant is content and asking nothing from them in either life.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r7.anchor: وجاء في فضلها ما أخرجه أبو موسى المديني في المعرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r8.claim: The sura follows the previous one by giving a reason for the Qur’an’s revelation: disbelievers would not leave disbelief until the proof, a messenger reciting purified pages, came to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200/r8.anchor: ووجه مناسبتها لما قبلها إن قوله تعالى فيها لم يكن الذين الخ كالتعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r1.claim: “Those who disbelieved from the People of the Book” means Jews and Christians; naming them this way may emphasize the gravity of their disbelief or signal their scriptural knowledge of the promised truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r1.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب أي اليهود والنصارى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r2.claim: The past-tense description treats their disbelief as arising after their prophets, in separate instances.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r2.anchor: وإيراد الصلة فعلا لما أن كفرهم حادث بعد أنبيائهم عليهم السلام بالآحاد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r3.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r3.claim: Al-Maturidi takes “min” partitively, not as explanatory, since some Christians, including Melkites, remained in true belief until Muhammad’s mission or their deaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r3.anchor: ومن للتبعيض كما قال علم الهدى الشيخ أبو منصور الماتريدي في التأويلات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r4.claim: The objection that explanatory “min” entails all had disbelieved beforehand is answered by identifying them as disbelievers in light of their state after the mission.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض لا نسلم أن التبيين يقتضي كفر جميعهم قبل البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas takes the People of the Book here as the Jewish tribes around Medina: Qurayza, al-Nadir, and Qaynuqaʿ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r5.anchor: وأيد إرادة التبعيض بما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r6.claim: The polytheists are those who assign God a partner, an idol or other being; some restrict the referent to idol-worshipping Arab polytheists around Mecca and Medina, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r6.anchor: والمشركين وهم من اعتقدوا الله سبحانه شريكا صنما أو غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r7.claim: Taking “the polytheists” as the People of the Book because they call Jesus or Ezra God’s son, coordinated only by a difference in label, is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r7.anchor: واحتمال أن يراد بالمشركين أهل الكتاب وشركهم لقولهم المسيح ابن الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r8.claim: A reading nominates “al-mushrikun” in coordination with the relative pronoun; parsing the common genitive reading as mere attraction is also discussed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r8.anchor: وقريء والمشركون بالرفع عطفا على الموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r9.claim: The phrase “from the People of the Book and the polytheists” functions circumstantially with “disbelieved.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r9.anchor: والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال من ضمير كفروا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r10.claim: “Munfakkin” is the predicate of “yakun”; it means leaving the state they held, and is the active participle of intransitive “infakka.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r10.anchor: وقوله تعالى منفكيم خبر يكن والأنفكاك في الأصل افتراق الأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r11.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r11.claim: Some grammarians derive the participle from defective “infakka” and posit an omitted predicate such as promising to follow truth; al-Alusi objects that a kāna predicate cannot ordinarily be omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r11.anchor: وزعم بعض النحاة أنه وصف منها والخبر محذوف أي واعدين اتباع الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r12.claim: “Until the clear proof comes” attaches to “munfakkin”; “bayyina” may mean one who makes truth clear or a proof establishing a claim, understood as a miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p200#2/r12.anchor: والبينة صفة اسم الفاعل أي المبين للحق أو هي بمعناها المعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the passage among the Qur’an’s hardest in structure and exegesis: reading it as pre-mission disbelief seems to say they stopped disbelieving when the Messenger came, contrary to what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r10.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظما وتفسيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r1.speaker: جار الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r1.claim: Zamakhshari says both groups claimed they would not leave their religions until the promised Prophet described in Torah and Gospel arrived; the next verse rebukes them for then separating from truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r1.anchor: قال جار الله كان الكفار من الفريقين يقولون قبل المبعث لا ننفك عما نحن فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r4.claim: A related reading says they kept their pledge to believe in the promised last messenger until the condition they had set arrived, as the following verse describes their division.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r4.anchor: أي لم يكونوا منفكين عما كانوا عليه من الوعد باتباع الحق والإيمان بالرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r5.claim: The People of the Book were known to seek victory through the coming Prophet; some polytheists may have accepted this belief, including Zayd ibn ʿAmr, who sought an Arab prophet from Quraysh and Hashim.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r5.anchor: حتى أنهم كانوا يستفتحون ويقولون اللهم افتح علينا وانصرنا بالنبي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r6.claim: The present form “comes” reflects the tense of the reported claim, as in a Qur’anic expression using a present verb for a past event.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r6.anchor: والتعبير عن إتيانه بصيغة المضارع حال المحكي لا باعتبار حال الحكاية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r8.claim: Although both groups had agreed in the prior claim, “not breaking away” describes their common position ending, while “separating” describes its fracture into their longstanding differences.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p202/r8.anchor: عبر عما صدر منهم عقيب الأتفاق عند الأخبار بوقوعه بالأنفكاك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r1.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r1.claim: Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar reads: they did not cease disbelieving even when the proof came. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi objects that “until” cannot mean “even though” in Arabic; an omitted “at any time” is also problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r1.anchor: وقال القاضي عبد الجبار المعنى لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين عن كفرهم وإن جاءتهم البينة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r2.claim: Another view says they praised the Prophet until he came, then split and spoke falsely about him; al-Alusi objects that this assumes an unstated complement for “not ceasing.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين عن ذكر الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالمناقب والفضائل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r3.claim: Some say the Prophet’s arrival made some believe and others persist, satisfying the endpoint; al-Alusi objects that the next verse condemns all and explicitly speaks of disbelievers among them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r3.anchor: ويكفي ذلك في العمل بموجب حتى وتعقب بأن ظاهر وما تفرق الخ ذم لجميعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r4.claim: Another view says they were certain in their religions until the Prophet came, when their thoughts became unsettled and doubtful; al-Alusi finds this unsatisfactory.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين عن كفرهم بأن يترددوا فيه بل كانوا جازمين به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r5.claim: A lexical interpretation makes “munfakkin” mean destroyed, by analogy with a childbirth injury; it yields that they were not punished or alive only until proof came, which al-Alusi dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r5.anchor: وقيل معنى منفكين هالكين من قولهم انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r6.claim: Another interpretation says they did not leave their religion until the Messenger’s pages showed its abrogation, after which they only adhered to it outwardly; al-Alusi says it is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد أنهم لم ينفكوا عن دينهم حقيقة إلى مجيء الرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says the groups remained together in their distinct religions until the proof came, then separated as each asserted its own position; al-Alusi objects that the proof should have united them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان الظاهر أن المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين أي منفصلا بعضهم عن بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya proposes that people were never outside God’s command, power, and oversight before a messenger was sent, since people are not left purposeless.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ههنا وجه بارع المعنى وذلك أن يكون المراد لم يكن هؤلاء القوم منفكين من أمر الله تعالى وقدرته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r9.speaker: القائلون بمفهوم الغاية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r9.claim: The apparent contradiction assumes that an endpoint implies a changed state afterward, a principle held by most jurists and theologians including Qadi Abu Bakr, Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r9.anchor: مبني على مذهب القائلين بمفهوم الغاية وهم أكثر الفقهاء وجماعة من المتكلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r10.speaker: أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r10.claim: Hanafis and other jurists and theologians deny that an endpoint carries this implication; al-Amidi chose their position and argued against opposing evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p203/r10.anchor: دون مذهب القائلين به وهم أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة وجماعة من الفقهاء والمتكلمين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.claim: People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are idol worshippers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.anchor: وهم اليهود والنصارى، {والمشركين} وهم عبدة الأوثان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.claim: Munfakkin means ceasing from unbelief and idolatry; language scholars also gloss it as departing or separating, with fakaktu as an example.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r2.anchor: منتهين عن كفرهم وشركهم، وقال أهل اللغة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r3.claim: The future wording means the proof had already come: Muhammad brought the Qur'an, clarified their error and ignorance, and called them to faith; some of both groups believed and were saved from misguidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r3.anchor: لفظه مستقبل ومعناه الماضي، أي: حتى أتتهم البينة، الحجة الواضحة، يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، أتاهم بالقرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r3.speaker: بعض أئمة اللغة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r3.claim: Some language authorities say munfakkin means perishing, using an idiom for a pelvic bone separating during birth and causing death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أئمة اللغة: معنى قوله "منفكين": هالكين، من قولهم: انفك [صلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r4.claim: On this less preferred interpretation, the unbelievers were not doomed or punished until proof was established by a messenger and scripture; Baghawi says the first interpretation is sounder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#3/r4.anchor: ومعنى الآية: لم يكونوا هالكين معذبين إلا من بعد قيام الحجة عليهم بإرسال الرسول وإنزال الكتاب، والأول أصح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.claim: The Prophet said God commanded him to recite this sura to Ubayy; when Ubayy asked whether he had been named, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي: "إن الله تعالى أمرني أن أقرأ عليك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.claim: A variant from Qatada says the command was for the Prophet to recite the Qur'an to Ubayy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.anchor: وقال همام عن قتادة: "أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r1.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians, whose disbelief is deviation concerning God's attributes; min is explanatory, and the polytheists are idol worshippers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r1.anchor: اليهود والنصارى فإنهم كفروا بالإلحاد في صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r2.claim: Munfakkin may mean that they would not abandon their religion, or that they would not abandon their pledge to follow the truth when the Messenger came.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r2.anchor: عما كانوا عليه من دينهم، أو الوعد باتباع الحق إذ جاءهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r3.claim: The clear proof may be the Messenger himself or the Quran, which makes the truth clear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r3.anchor: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أو القرآن، فإنه مبين للحق

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r4.claim: The clear proof may be the Messenger's miraculous character and the Quran's silencing of anyone who challenges it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:1-6/r4.anchor: معجزة الرسول بأخلاقه والقرآن بإفحامه من تحدى به

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever recites this surah will be with the best of creation at the evening resting place on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة لم يكن الذين كفروا كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية مساء ومقيلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r1.claim: As the hidden descent and identity of the blessed night last until dawn, people of every religion normally change only through a proof clearer than dawn; the Qur'an and its messenger are that decisive proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r1.anchor: لم يصح في العادة الجارية على حكمة الأسباب في دار الأسباب أن يتحولوا عما هم فيه إلا بسبب عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r2.claim: “They were not to desist” spans past, present, and future as a settled disposition, unlike the earlier habit of changing among disbelief and innovation without remaining firm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r2.anchor: في مطلق الزمان الماضي والحال والاستقبال كونا هو كالجبلة والطبع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r3.claim: After Moses the Israelites repeatedly became blind and deaf and repented, then relapsed; the verse describing this is evidence for their instability.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r3.anchor: كما دل على بعض ذلك قوله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r4.claim: Arab polytheists shifted among worshipping idols, angels, and jinn rather than holding one belief; after the proof of Islam, converts abandoned pre-Islamic practices such as gambling and the customs of sāʾiba.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r4.anchor: وتارة يبعدون الأصنام , وتارة الملائكة , وأخرى الجن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r5.claim: The People of the Book are mentioned first because they knew revelation and bore greater responsibility; they altered and distorted their originally true religion, so God replaced their legal details while preserving agreement on fundamentals.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r5.anchor: بدأ بقوله : { من أهل الكتاب } أي من اليهود والنصارى الذين كان أصل دينهم حقا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r6.claim: The polytheists worshipped idols, fire, the sun, and similar things; the author describes them as wholly detached from their former religion and invokes their prior expectation of a coming messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p495/r6.anchor: أي بعبادة الأصنام والنار والشمس ونحو ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r1.claim: The imperfect verb presents the proof as renewed continually through recurring messengers and recitation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r1.anchor: عبر بالمضارع لتجدد البيان في كل وقت بتجدد الرسال والتلاوة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r2.claim: The bayyina is the Messenger together with his signs, above all the revealed Book, whether Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r2.anchor: وذلك هو الرسول وما معه من الآيات التي أعظمها الكتاب سواء كان التوراة أو الإنجيل أو الزبور أو الفرقان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r7.claim: Before the proof arrived, People of the Book believed in the Prophet because of explicit glad tidings, while polytheists claimed a warner would make them better guided; his arrival divided both groups into believers and rejecters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r7.anchor: أهل الكتاب يؤمنون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما عندهم من البشائر الصريحة به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r8.claim: The surah continues the prior account of reciting the Book and the night of its revelation, stressing that Jews had invoked and praised the promised Book and messenger but became its first rejecters when they appeared.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r8.anchor: هي من كمال ما تقدمها لأنه لما أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام بقراءة كتابه الذي به اتضحت سبيله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p497/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p497/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p497/r1.claim: The Book and its bearer had been foretold in Torah and Gospel, and People of the Book had hoped to gain victory over their enemies through him; those without prior knowledge, such as Abu Bakr and Umar, were blessed for accepting him, whereas informed rejecters became the worst creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p497/r1.anchor: وقد كانوا يؤملون الانتصار به عليه الصلاة والسلام من أعدائهم ويستفتحون بكتابه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r1.claim: One who fears God leaves whatever is unfitting for Him, does not doubt the proof, and keeps fear in the heart, which the surah links back to its opening division between those who escape desire and those ruined by it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r1.anchor: فمن خاف ربه هذا الخوف انفك من جميع ما عنده مما لا يليق بجنابه سبحانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r2.claim: The surah divides people into one group freed from the soul's desire and saved, and another remaining its captive and destroyed.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r3.claim: The author's prior account says the Prophet specifically recited this surah to Ubayy after a reading dispute with two Companions; their readings were approved, and Ubayy then felt a doubt more severe than his pre-Islamic doubt.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r3.anchor: أنه وجد اثنين من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قد خالفاه في القراءة فرفعهما إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r4.claim: Ubayy says the Prophet struck his chest, he broke into a sweat, and the Prophet explained that the Qur'an was revealed in seven aḥruf.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r4.anchor: فضرب صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدري ففضت عرقا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r5.claim: The disputed reading occurred in al-Naḥl, whose themes this short surah condenses: prophetic witness, the Book's guidance and mercy, Gabriel strengthening believers, and the Jews' disagreement over Sabbath; Bayyina also warns against doubt after clear proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r5.anchor: على قصرها حاوية إجمالا لكل ما في النحل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r6.claim: The Prophet's concise reminder helped Ubayy grasp the warning quickly and retain it deeply, and God granted him steadfastness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r6.anchor: ليكون أسرع له تصورا فيكون أرسخ في النفس وأثبت في القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r7.claim: The Prophet called Ubayy the most proficient reciter; Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it from Anas, the author grades it authentic, and some transmit it mursal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r7.anchor: رواه أحمد والترمذي وابن ماجه عن أنس رضي الله تعالى عنه وهو صحيح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r8.claim: The author warns that status should not prevent learning from someone of lower rank; many People of the Book rejected Islam because they compared their scriptural learning with the Arabs' ignorance rather than their present message.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p502/r8.anchor: حتى لا يمنع أحدا ما يراه من علوه من القراءة على من هو دونه

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r1.claim: The author classifies al-Bayyina as Medinan and counts eight verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r2.claim: He says the chapter ‘Lam yakun’ was revealed in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة {لم يكن} بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r3.claim: She disagrees and says the chapter was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: نزلت سورة {لم يكن} بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r4.claim: A report says God hears recitation of the chapter and promises its reader a place in Paradise until satisfied.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r4.anchor: عن اسماعيل بن أبي حكيم المزني أحد بني فضيل: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن الله ليسمع قراءة {لم يكن}

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r5.claim: A variant report promises that God will never forget the reader in worldly or afterlife circumstances and will grant a place in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r5.anchor: عن اسماعيل بن أبي حكيم عن مطر المزني أو المدني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله ليسمع قراءة {لم يكن الذين كفروا}

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r6.claim: When this passage was revealed, Gabriel told the Prophet that God commanded him to recite it to Ubayy; Ubayy later wept when the Prophet confirmed this.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r6.anchor: عن أبي حبة البدري قال: لما نزلت {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب} إلى آخرها قال جبريل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r7.claim: Anas says God commanded the Prophet to recite the chapter to Ubayy and had named him specifically, prompting Ubayy to weep.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك {لم يكن الذين كفروا}

DURR-FULL:v8p585/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r8.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r8.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet's recitation to him, including a statement that human greed continues even if granted successive valleys, death fills the belly, repentance is accepted, and true religion is pure monotheism rather than polytheism, Judaism, or Christianity.
DURR-FULL:v8p585/r8.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب}

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.claim: Ubayy reported that God ordered the Prophet to recite the opening of al-Bayyina to him, followed by statements identifying the true religion as non-polytheist hanifiyya and promising that good is not denied.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.anchor: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك فقرأ علي

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.claim: A second Ubayy report presents an expanded recitation with explanations of upright religion, righteous deeds, the best and worst of creation, and the recompense of the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.anchor: إن أقوم الدين الحنيفية مسلمة غير مشركة

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recalled the Prophet's saying that Adam would seek a third valley of gold after two, and that only dust fills his belly; God accepts repentance.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.anchor: لو كان لابن آدم واديان من ذهب لابتغى الثالث

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.claim: Ubayy affirmed that the Prophet had taught him the disputed wording; Umar asked whether to enter it in the codex, and Ubayy did not forbid him.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.anchor: هكذا اقرأنيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Ubayy quoted the two-valley saying, and Umar asked whether it should be written; Ubayy said he would not forbid it, while remaining unsure whether it was revelation or Prophetic speech.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.anchor: فكأن أبيا شك أقول من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قرآن منزل

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r3.claim: Mujahid said that when the surah was revealed, God told the Prophet to recite it to Ubayy, who asked whether God had commanded this and agreed when told yes.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r3.anchor: لما نزلت {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب}

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.claim: Qatada glossed منفكين as ceasing their state, the Bayyina as this Qur'an, and the purified pages as the Qur'an praised in the finest terms.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين} قال: منتهي عما هم فيه

DURR-FULL:v8p588/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj identified the Bayyina as Muhammad and glossed دين القيمة as the upright religion.
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {حتى تأتيهم البينة} قال: محمد وفي قوله: {وذلك دين القيمة} قال: القيم

DURR-FULL:v8p588/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r7.speaker: أبو واثل
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r7.claim: Abu Wa'il answered questions about faith by reciting the passage from the disbelievers of the Book through sincere worship.
DURR-FULL:v8p588/r7.anchor: كان أبو واثل إذا سئل عن شيء من الإيمان قرأ

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Makkan according to the majority, as first reported here.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār say the sūra is Medinan, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار : مدنية ، قاله ابن عطية

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r3.speaker: كتاب التحرير
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r3.claim: The book al-Taḥrīr calls the sūra Medinan and says this is the majority view.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r3.anchor: وفي كتاب التحرير : مدنية ، وهو قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r4.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s view that the sūra is Makkan.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r4.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنها مكية

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r5.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r5.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām chose the reported Makkan classification.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r5.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنها مكية ، واختاره يحيى بن سلام

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r6.claim: Following the previous sūra’s mention of Quranic revelation and the command Read in your Lord’s name, this sūra says disbelievers persisted until the Messenger recited the revealed pages.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r6.anchor: لما ذكر إنزال القرآن ، وفي السورة التي قبلها { اقرأ باسم ربك } ذكر هنا أن الكفار

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r7.claim: The verse divides the disbelievers into People of Scripture and people of associationism.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r7.anchor: وقسم الكافرين هنا إلى أهل كتاب وأهل إشراك

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r8.speaker: بعض القراء
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r8.claim: Some readers put al-mushrikūn in the nominative, coordinating it with all who disbelieved.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r8.anchor: وقرأ بعض القراء : والمشركون رفعاً عطفاً على { الذين كفروا }

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r9.claim: The majority read al-mushrikīn in the genitive, coordinating it with People of Scripture.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r9.anchor: والجمهور : بالجر عطفاً على { أهل الكتاب }

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r10.claim: People of Scripture are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are Arab idol worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r10.anchor: وأهل الكتاب اليهود والنصارى ، والمشركون عبدة الأوثان من العرب

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the People of Scripture as Yathrib’s Jews—Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr, and Banū Qaynuqāʿ—and the polytheists as those around Mecca and Medina.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أهل الكتاب اليهود الذين كانوا بيثرب هم قريظة والنضير وبنو قينقاع ، والمشركون

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r12.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r12.claim: Mujāhid and others understand that they persisted in unbelief and error until the clear proof came.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r12.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره : لم يكونوا منفكين عن الكفر والضلال حتى جاءتهم البينة

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r13.speaker: الفراء وغيره
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others say they kept recognizing Muhammad’s prophethood as true and awaiting his command until the proof came, whereupon they split.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء وغيره : لم يكونوا منفكين عن معرفة صحة نبوّة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والتوكف لأمره حتى جاءتهم البينة ، فتفرقوا

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r14.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says both groups had claimed before Muhammad’s mission that they would keep their religions until the promised prophet foretold in Torah and Gospel came; God recounts their claim.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r14.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : كان الكفار من الفريقين يقولون قبل المبعث : لا ننفك مما نحن فيه من ديننا حتى يبعث النبي الموعود

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r15.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya proposes that people remain under God’s command, power, and care until He sends a warning messenger to establish proof and complete favor for believers; they are not left purposeless.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : ويتجه في معنى الآية قول ثالث بارع المعنى ، وذلك أنه يكون المراد : لم يكن هؤلاء القوم منفكين من أمر الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r16.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r16.claim: An unnamed view takes the phrase to mean that they would not cease living and die until the proof came.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r16.anchor: وقيل : لم يكونوا منفكين عن حياتهم فيموتوا حتى تأتيهم البينة

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r17.claim: The apparent sense is that the groups did not separate from one another: each accepted the other’s chosen belief, and their affection and unity lasted until the proof came.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r17.anchor: والظاهر أن المعنى : لم يكونوا منفكين ، أي منفصلاً بعضهم من بعض

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r18.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r18.claim: Another view reads munfakkīn as perishing, drawing on an expression for a part separating during childbirth; it means they were not punished or destroyed before proof through messengers and books.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r18.anchor: وقيل : معنى منفكين : هالكين ، من قولهم : انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r19.claim: Abū Ḥayyān parses munfakkīn as the active participle of complete intransitive infakka, not the defective verb taking a subject and predicate.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r19.anchor: ومنفكين اسم فاعل من انفك ، وهي التامة وليست الداخلة على المبتدأ والخبر

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r20.speaker: بعض النحاة
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r20.claim: Some grammarians treat infakka as defective and supply an omitted predicate such as knowing Muhammad’s affair.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r20.anchor: وقال بعض النحاة : هي الناقصة ، ويقدر منفكين : عارفين أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r21.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that parse because, according to his school, the predicate of kāna and its sisters cannot be omitted either by ellipsis or abbreviation.
