ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r21.anchor: وخبر كان وأخواتها لا يجوز حذفه لا اقتصاراً ولا اختصاراً ، نص على ذلك أصحابنا

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r22.claim: He notes a poetic example where the predicate in ḥīna laysa mujīr is understood as fī al-dunyā, but says this deletion is forced by poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r22.anchor: وقالوا في قوله : حين ليس مجير ، أي في الدنيا ، فحذف الخبر أنه ضرورة

ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r23.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r23.claim: Al-bayyina means a manifest, decisive proof.
ABUHAYYAN:98:1/r23.anchor: فحذف الخبر أنه ضرورة ، والبينة : الحجة الجليلة

ALUSI:98:1/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r1.claim: The sūra is also called al-Qiyāma, al-Balad, al-Munfakkin, al-Bariyya, and Lam Yakun, as well as al-Bayyina.
ALUSI:98:1/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة القيامة وسورة البلد وسورة المنفكين وسورة البرية وسورة لم يكن

ALUSI:98:1/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:98:1/r2.claim: Al-Bahr reports that the majority consider the sūra Meccan.
ALUSI:98:1/r2.anchor: قال في البحر مكية في قول الجمهور

ALUSI:98:1/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار
ALUSI:98:1/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Ata ibn Yasar are reported by Ibn Atiyya to consider the sūra Medinan.
ALUSI:98:1/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار مدنية قاله ابن عطية

ALUSI:98:1/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r4.speaker: كتاب التحرير
ALUSI:98:1/r4.claim: Kitab al-Tahrir calls the sūra Medinan and says this is the majority position, contrary to Al-Bahr's report of a Meccan majority.
ALUSI:98:1/r4.anchor: وفي كتاب التحرير مدنية وهو قول الجمهور

ALUSI:98:1/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
ALUSI:98:1/r5.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that the sūra is Meccan; Yahya ibn Sallam chooses that view.
ALUSI:98:1/r5.anchor: وروي أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنها مكية واختاره يحيى بن سلام

ALUSI:98:1/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r6.speaker: ابن الفرس
ALUSI:98:1/r6.claim: Ibn al-Faris says the more widely known position is that the sūra is Meccan; Ibn Mardawayh also transmits this from Aisha.
ALUSI:98:1/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الفرس الأشهر إنها مكية ورواه ابن مردويه عن عائشة

ALUSI:98:1/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI:98:1/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir decisively considers the sūra Medinan, citing the report that Gabriel instructed the Prophet to recite it to Ubayy ibn Kab.
ALUSI:98:1/r7.anchor: وجزم ابن كثير بأنها مدنية واستدل على ذلك بما أخرجه الإمام أحمد

ALUSI:98:1/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r8.speaker: أبو خيثمة البدري
ALUSI:98:1/r8.claim: Abu Khaythama al-Badri reports that Gabriel told the Prophet God commanded him to recite the sūra to Ubayy; Ubayy asked if named, heard yes, and wept. Al-Ālūsī calls this sounder. No grading is stated.
ALUSI:98:1/r8.anchor: عن أبي خيثمة البدري قال لما نزلت لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب إلى آخرها

ALUSI:98:1/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r9.claim: The sūra has nine verses in the Basran count and eight in other verse-counting traditions.
ALUSI:98:1/r9.anchor: وآيها تسع في البصري وثمان في غيره

ALUSI:98:1/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r10.speaker: مطر المزني أو المدني
ALUSI:98:1/r10.claim: Matar al-Muzani, or al-Madani, transmits a Prophetic merit report: God hears this sūra's recitation and promises reward and a place in Paradise until contentment. No grading is stated.
ALUSI:98:1/r10.anchor: عن مطر المزني أو المدني عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال إن الله تعالى يسمع قراءة لم يكن الذين كفروا

ALUSI:98:1/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r11.claim: The opening explains the Qur'an's revelation: the disbelievers would not desist until the Messenger came reciting purified pages, which is what was revealed.
ALUSI:98:1/r11.anchor: إن قوله تعالى فيها لم يكن الذين الخ كالتعليل لإنزال القرآن

ALUSI:98:1/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r12.claim: Ahl al-Kitab means Jews and Christians; the title either stresses the enormity of their unbelief or hints that they should follow truth found in their scriptures.
ALUSI:98:1/r12.anchor: أي اليهود والنصارى وإيرادهم بذلك العنوان قيل لإعظام شناعة كفرهم

ALUSI:98:1/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r13.claim: The relative clause uses a past verb because their unbelief arose after their prophets, through later deviations concerning God's attributes.
ALUSI:98:1/r13.anchor: وإيراد الصلة فعلاً لما أن كفرهم حادث بعد أنبيائهم عليهم السلام بالآحاد

ALUSI:98:1/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r14.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
ALUSI:98:1/r14.claim: Abu Mansur al-Maturidi takes min as partitive, not explanatory: some people of the Book remained in true belief until death; explanatory min would imply all disbelieved before the mission.
ALUSI:98:1/r14.anchor: ومن للتبعيض كما قال علم الهدى الشيخ أبو منصور الماتريدي في التأويلات لا للتبيين

ALUSI:98:1/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:98:1/r15.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the intended people of the Book as Jews around Medina: Banu Qurayza, al-Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa.
ALUSI:98:1/r15.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بأهل الكتاب اليهود

ALUSI:98:1/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r16.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:98:1/r16.claim: Another view denies that explanatory min entails all were unbelievers before the mission, since 'those who disbelieved' could describe their state after the mission.
ALUSI:98:1/r16.anchor: وقال بعض لا نسلم أن التبيين يقتضي كفر جميعهم قبل البعث

ALUSI:98:1/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r17.claim: The polytheists are those who assign a partner to God, whether an idol or something else.
ALUSI:98:1/r17.anchor: وهم من اعتقدوا لله سبحانه شريكاً صنماً أو غيره

ALUSI:98:1/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r18.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:98:1/r18.claim: Some restrict the intended polytheists to idol worshippers, since that described Arab polytheists around Mecca and Medina; this is attributed to Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI:98:1/r18.anchor: وخصهم بعض بعبدة الأصنام لأن مشركي العرب الذين بمكة والمدينة

ALUSI:98:1/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r19.claim: The polytheists are coordinated with Ahl al-Kitab; partitive min does not require some of the combined group to be non-disbelievers, since it can qualify a subset of the whole.
ALUSI:98:1/r19.anchor: فالعطف على أهل الكتاب ولا يلزم على التبعيض أن لا يكون بعضهم كافرين

ALUSI:98:1/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r20.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:98:1/r20.claim: An interpretation including the people of the Book among polytheists because they call Christ or Ezra God's son, coordinated only by label, is rejected as untenable.
ALUSI:98:1/r20.anchor: واحتمال أن يراد بالمشركين أهل الكتاب وشركهم لقولهم المسيح ابن الله

ALUSI:98:1/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r21.speaker: قارئ
ALUSI:98:1/r21.claim: A variant reads al-mushrikūna in the nominative, coordinated with the relative pronoun; the majority accusative form cannot be explained as a genitive by adjacency.
ALUSI:98:1/r21.anchor: وقرئ والمشركون بالرفع عطفاً على الموصول

ALUSI:98:1/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r22.claim: The prepositional phrase min ahl al-kitab functions circumstantially with the pronoun in kafaru.
ALUSI:98:1/r22.anchor: والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال من ضمير كفروا

ALUSI:98:1/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r23.claim: Infikak originally means separation of things joined together; here munfakkin means parting from the state they held, as explained later.
ALUSI:98:1/r23.anchor: والانفكاك في الأصل افتراق الأمور الملتحمة بنوع مزايلة

ALUSI:98:1/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r24.claim: Munfakkin is yakun's predicate and an active participle from complete intransitive انفك; one grammarian instead supplies an omitted predicate from the deficient verb, which Al-Ālūsī criticizes as impermissible without necessity.
ALUSI:98:1/r24.anchor: فالوصف اسم فاعل من انفك التامة دون الناقصة الداخلة على المبتدأ والخبر

ALUSI:98:1/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:1/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:1/r25.claim: The until-clause attaches to munfakkin; bayyina can mean one who clarifies truth or the familiar proof establishing a claim, here a miracle.
ALUSI:98:1/r25.anchor: متعلق بمنفكين والبينة صفة بمعنى اسم الفاعل أي المبين للحق

ALUSI:98:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r2.claim: If bayyina means the Prophet who clarifies truth, identifying the proof with him is straightforward; if it means proof, his qualities are miraculous, as al-Ghazali and al-Busiri indicate, alongside other manifest miracles.
ALUSI:98:3/r2.anchor: وإطلاق البينة عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام على المعنى الأول ظاهر وعلى المعنى الأخير باعتبار أن أخلاقه وصفاته

ALUSI:98:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r3.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI:98:3/r3.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd are reported to take al-bayyina as the Qur'an, because it clarifies truth or is a miraculous proof establishing the claim.
ALUSI:98:3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالبينة القرآن لأنه مبين للحق أو معجز مثبت للمدعي وروي ذلك عن قتادة وابن زيد

ALUSI:98:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r13.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI:98:3/r13.claim: Al-Wahidi calls this one of the Qur'an's hardest passages in syntax and interpretation: if both groups disbelieved before the mission, the apparent sense says the Messenger's arrival ended their disbelief, contrary to history and 98:4, which says the people of the Book split only after the proof came.
ALUSI:98:3/r13.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظماً وتفسيراً

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r1.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet said God commanded him to recite the Quran to him, then recited the opening of Sura al-Bayyina and sayings on wealth, repentance, monotheism, and reward.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21202/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن

BAGHAWI:98:1/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:1/r1.claim: The sura is Medinan and has eight verses.

BAGHAWI:98:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:1/r2.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians, while the associators are idol worshippers.
BAGHAWI:98:1/r2.anchor: { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب } وهم اليهود والنصارى ، { والمشركين } وهم عبدة الأوثان

BAGHAWI:98:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:1/r3.claim: Munfakkīn means departing, separating, or coming apart; the Arabic usage is “I freed the thing, and it came apart.”
BAGHAWI:98:1/r3.anchor: { منفكين } زائلين منفصلين ، يقال : فككت الشيء فانفك ، أي : انفصل

BAGHAWI:98:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:1/r4.claim: Although phrased as future, the clause means until the clear proof had come: Muhammad brought the Quran, exposed their errors and ignorance, and called them to Islam and faith; members of both groups who believed were thereby saved from error.
BAGHAWI:98:1/r4.anchor: لفظه مستقبل ومعناه الماضي ، أي : حتى أتتهم الحجة الواضحة ، يعني : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أتاهم بالقرآن

BAYDAWI:98:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:1/r1.claim: The sūra's place of revelation is disputed, and it has eight verses.
BAYDAWI:98:1/r1.anchor: سورة البينة مختلف فيها ، وآيها ثماني آيات .

BAYDAWI:98:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:1/r2.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians, who disbelieved by denying or deviating in God's attributes; min is explanatory.
BAYDAWI:98:1/r2.anchor: اليهود والنصارى فإنهم كفروا بالإلحاد في صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى ،

BAYDAWI:98:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:1/r3.claim: The polytheists are the idol worshippers.

BAYDAWI:98:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:1/r4.claim: Munfakkīn may mean they would not leave their religion, or would not abandon the promise to follow the truth when the Messenger came.
BAYDAWI:98:1/r4.anchor: منفكين عما كانوا عليه من دينهم ، أو الوعد باتباع الحق إذ جاءهم الرسول

BAYDAWI:98:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:1/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:1/r5.claim: The clear proof may be the Messenger, the Qur'an that makes truth clear, or the Messenger's character as a miracle and the Qur'an's power to silence challengers.
BAYDAWI:98:1/r5.anchor: حتى تأتيهم البينة } الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أو القرآن ؛ فإنه مبين للحق ، أو معجزة الرسول بأخلاقه

BIQAI:98:1/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r1.claim: Following the account of the hidden, honored night whose clarity arrives with dawn, this sūra says religious communities would not change until an even clearer proof came.
BIQAI:98:1/r1.anchor: أخبر سبحانه وتعالى أن الليلة الشريفة التي صانها بنوع خفاء في تنزل من يتنزل فيها

BIQAI:98:1/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r2.claim: In the regular order of causes, people of religions, whether originally true or not, do not leave their positions without a cause clearer than dawn: the Qurʾān and its Messenger.
BIQAI:98:1/r2.anchor: في العادة الجارية على حكمة الأسباب في دار الأسباب

BIQAI:98:1/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r3.claim: The wording covers past, present, and future as a habitual condition, portraying their unstable religious changes as an ingrained pattern.
BIQAI:98:1/r3.anchor: في مطلق الزمان الماضي والحال والاستقبال كوناً هو كالجبلة والطبع

BIQAI:98:1/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r4.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians whose religion originated in truth but who distorted it and deviated in describing God; revelation later abrogated their changed branches while retaining agreement on fundamentals.
BIQAI:98:1/r4.anchor: أي من اليهود والنصارى الذين كان أصل دينهم حقاً

BIQAI:98:1/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r5.claim: The polytheists worshipped idols, fire, the sun, and similar things, and had no revealed scripture or original basis in truth.
BIQAI:98:1/r5.anchor: أي بعبادة الأصنام والنار والشمس ونحو ذلك

BIQAI:98:1/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r6.claim: Here munfakkīn means completely severed from and released from their former religion, with no remaining attachment, and remaining in that separated state.
BIQAI:98:1/r6.anchor: أي منفصلين زائلين عما كانوا عليه من دينهم

BIQAI:98:1/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r7.claim: The root f-k-k conveys opening and separating what had been joined, as in freeing a book, seal, or bone.
BIQAI:98:1/r7.anchor: وأصل الفك الفتح والانفصال لما كان ملتحماً ، من فك الكتاب والختم والعظم

BIQAI:98:1/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r8.claim: Alternatively, the phrase concerns abandoning their expectation of following truth when its promised messenger arrived; the People of the Book sought victory through him and the polytheists swore they would be better guided than other nations.
BIQAI:98:1/r8.anchor: أو عما في أنفسهم من ظن اتباع الحق إذا جاءهم الرسول المبشر به بما كان أهل الكتاب يستفتحون به ، والمشركون يقسمون بالله جهد أيمانهم

BIQAI:98:1/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r9.claim: The polytheists’ oath was that if a warner came, they would be more rightly guided than any of the nations; this expectation is cited from the Qurʾān.
BIQAI:98:1/r9.anchor: لئن جاءهم نذير ليكونن أهدى من إحدى الأمم

BIQAI:98:1/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r10.claim: The imperfect verb signals clarification recurring at each moment through renewed messengership and recitation.
BIQAI:98:1/r10.anchor: عبر بالمضارع لتجدد البيان في كل وقت بتجدد الرسالة والتلاوة

BIQAI:98:1/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:1/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:1/r11.claim: The clear proof is the Messenger together with his signs, especially the revealed Book, whether Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qurʾān.
BIQAI:98:1/r11.anchor: وذلك هو الرسول وما معه من الآيات التي أعظمها الكتاب سواء كان التوراة أو الإنجيل أو الزبور أو الفرقان

BIQAI:98:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:3/r3.claim: Before the proof, the People of the Book shared belief in the Prophet based on explicit glad tidings, and polytheists promised to follow a warner; when he came, they divided, with some believing and others disbelieving.
BIQAI:98:3/r3.anchor: فإذا أتتهم هذه البينة انفكوا ، وانفكاكهم أنهم كانوا مجتمعين قبل هذا ، أهل الكتاب يؤمنون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما عندهم من البشائر الصريحة به

BIQAI:98:3/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:98:3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Jews had anticipated the promised Book and Messenger and expected to prevail through him, but when the promise became visible they were the first to reject him.
BIQAI:98:3/r5.anchor: هذا الكتاب هو الذي كانت اليهود تستفتح به على مشركي العرب ، وتعظم أمره وأمر الآتي به ، حتى إذا حصل ذلك مشاهداً لهم كانوا هم أول كافر به

DURR:98:1/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:98:1/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sura was revealed in Medina.
DURR:98:1/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت سورة { لم يكن } بالمدينة

DURR:98:1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR:98:1/r2.claim: Aisha says the sura was revealed in Mecca, differing from Ibn Abbas's Medinan report.
DURR:98:1/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : نزلت سورة { لم يكن } بمكة

DURR:98:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:98:1/r3.claim: Ismail ibn Abi Hakim al-Muzani reports the Prophet saying God hears recitation of this sura and promises the reciter a place in Paradise until contentment.
DURR:98:1/r3.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أبي حكيم المزني أحد بني فضيل : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : «إن الله ليسمع قراءة

DURR:98:1/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:98:1/r4.claim: A version through Matar al-Muzani or al-Madani says God will never forget the reciter in any worldly or afterlife circumstance and will grant him a place in Paradise until satisfied.
DURR:98:1/r4.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أبي حكيم ، عن مطر المزني أو المدني ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «إن الله ليسمع قراءة

DURR:98:1/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r5.speaker: أبو حبة البدري
DURR:98:1/r5.claim: Abu Hubba al-Badri reports that after the sura was revealed, Gabriel ordered the Prophet to have Ubayy recite it; when Ubayy asked if he had been named, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept.
DURR:98:1/r5.anchor: عن أبي حبة البدري قال : لما نزلت { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب } إلى آخرها

DURR:98:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR:98:1/r6.claim: Anas reports that God commanded the Prophet to recite the sura to Ubayy; when Ubayy asked whether he had been named, he was told yes and wept. Another wording says the Prophet summoned Ubayy after revelation and read it to him.
DURR:98:1/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب : «إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك { لم يكن الذين كفروا }

DURR:98:1/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:98:1/r7.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet was ordered to recite the Qur'an to him, including this sura and added material on Adam's greed, repentance, and the true religion; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:98:1/r7.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب }

DURR:98:1/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:98:1/r8.claim: A second Ubayy report gives the Prophet's recitation of the sura through the clear proof and includes extra wording on hanifiyya and good deeds; it then adds material about Adam's desire for wealth.
DURR:98:1/r8.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك فقرأ عليَّ { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب

DURR:98:1/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:98:1/r9.claim: In a longer Ubayy report, the Prophet's recitation also includes wording on the best and worst of creation, humanity's original unity, the sending of prophets, prayer, almsgiving, and the righteous person's reward.
DURR:98:1/r9.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «يا أبي إني أمرت أن أقرئك سورة

DURR:98:1/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:98:1/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Umar testing a man with forty camels; Ibn Abbas then cites Ubayy's recitation that Adam would seek a third valley of gold, only dust fills his belly, and God accepts repentance. Ubayy says the Prophet read it to him.
DURR:98:1/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : جاء رجل إلى عمر يسأله فجعل عمر ينظر إلى رأسه مرة وإلى رجليه أخرى

DURR:98:1/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:98:1/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says he asked Umar about Ubayy's claim that an ayah was left unwritten; Ubayy repeated the two-valleys saying, but seemed unsure whether it was a Prophetic saying or revealed Qur'an, and did not forbid writing it.
DURR:98:1/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قلت : يا أمير المؤمنين : إن أبياً يزعم أنك تركت من آيات الله آية لم تكتبها

DURR:98:1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:98:1/r12.claim: Mujahid reports that after the sura was revealed, the Prophet told Ubayy that God had ordered him to recite it; Ubayy asked whether God had commanded this, and the Prophet said yes.
DURR:98:1/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : لما نزلت { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب } لقي أبي بن كعب رسول الله

DURR:98:1/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR:98:1/r13.claim: Qatada glosses “munfakkin” as ceasing from their present state.
DURR:98:1/r13.anchor: عن قتادة { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين } قال : منتهين عما هم فيه

DURR:98:1/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:98:1/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “munfakkin” as departing or leaving off.
DURR:98:1/r14.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { منفكين } قال : برحين

DURR:98:1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r15.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:98:1/r15.claim: Mujahid says they would not believe until the truth became clear.
DURR:98:1/r15.anchor: عن مجاهد { منفكين } قال : منتهين ، لم يكونوا ليؤمنوا حتى تبين لهم الحق

DURR:98:1/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r16.speaker: قتادة
DURR:98:1/r16.claim: Qatada identifies the clear proof as the Qur'an.
DURR:98:1/r16.anchor: عن قتادة { لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين } قال : منتهين عما هم فيه { حتى تأتيهم البينة } أي هذا القرآن

DURR:98:1/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:98:1/r17.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR:98:1/r17.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the clear proof as Muhammad.
DURR:98:1/r17.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : { حتى تأتيهم البينة } قال : محمد

IBNASHUR:98:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNASHUR:98:1/r1.claim: Al-Bukhārī and Muslim report from Anas that the Prophet said God had commanded him to recite the sūrah to Ubayy; Ubayy asked whether he had been named and, told yes, wept. Its opening clause names the whole sūrah.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r1.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب

IBNASHUR:98:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r2.claim: The common title in tafsīr and hadith books is Sūrat Lam yakun, shortened to its first word; it is also the familiar name among Tunisian Qurʾān-school students.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r2.anchor: وسميت هذه السورة في معظم كتب التفسير وكتب السنة

IBNASHUR:98:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r3.claim: The other recorded titles are al-Qayyima, al-Bayyina, Ahl al-Kitāb in Ubayy’s codex, al-Bariyya, and al-Infikāk, making six names in all.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r3.anchor: وسميت في أكثر المصاحف { سورة القيمة } وكذلك في بعض التفاسير

IBNASHUR:98:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:98:1/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the more widely held view is that the sūrah is Meccan, as most commentators say.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية : الأشهر أنها مكية وهو قول جمهور المفسرين

IBNASHUR:98:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r5.speaker: ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار
IBNASHUR:98:1/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār are reported to classify the sūrah as Medinan.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r5.anchor: وعن ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار هي مدنية

IBNASHUR:98:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r6.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR:98:1/r6.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reverses the attributions: he assigns the Medinan view to the majority and Ibn ʿAbbās, and the Meccan view to Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r6.anchor: وعكس القرطبي فنسب القول بأنها مدنية إلى الجمهور وابن عباس والقول بأنها مكية إلى يحيى بن سلام

IBNASHUR:98:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r7.speaker: أبو حبة البدري
IBNASHUR:98:1/r7.claim: Abū Ḥabba al-Badrī reports that when the passage was revealed Gabriel told the Prophet that God commanded him to recite it to Ubayy, supporting a Medinan setting.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن كثير عن أحمد بن حنبل بسنده إلى أبي حبة البدري قال

IBNASHUR:98:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r8.claim: Al-Baghawī and Ibn Kathīr firmly call it Medinan; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers this because it often rebukes the People of the Book and because of Abū Ḥabba’s report.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r8.anchor: وجزم البغوي وابن كثير بأنها مدنية

IBNASHUR:98:1/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r9.speaker: جابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR:98:1/r9.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd includes the sūrah among the Medinan revelations.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r9.anchor: وقد عدها جابر بن زيد في عداد السور المدنية

IBNASHUR:98:1/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:98:1/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues for a Medinan setting on the ground that the Prophet only confronted the People of the Book there.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية : إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما دفع إلى مناقضة أهل الكتاب بالدينة

IBNASHUR:98:1/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r11.claim: It ranks 101st in revelation, after al-Ṭalāq and before al-Ḥashr; since Banū al-Naḍīr was in Rabīʿ I, year four, it was revealed in late year three or early year four.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r11.anchor: وقد عدت المائة وإحدى في ترتيب النزول نزلت بعد سورة الطلاق وقبل سورة الحشر

IBNASHUR:98:1/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r12.claim: Most authorities count eight verses in the sūrah, while the people of Basra count nine.

IBNASHUR:98:1/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r13.claim: The sūrah rebukes the polytheists and People of the Book for rejecting the Qurʾān and the Messenger, and exposes the contradiction of awaiting the clear proof and then rejecting it.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r13.anchor: أغراضها توبيخ المشركين وأهل الكتاب على تكذيبهم بالقرآن والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r14.claim: Among the sūrah’s aims are to refute their claim that God required them to remain with their existing religions, warn them of the afterlife, and mark them as the worst creatures.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r14.anchor: وتكذيبهم في ادعائهم أن الله أوجب عليهم التمسك بالأديان التي هم عليها

IBNASHUR:98:1/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r15.claim: The sūrah praises believers who do good and promises them everlasting bliss, God’s approval, and whatever will satisfy them.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r15.anchor: والثناء على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

IBNASHUR:98:1/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r16.claim: It also extols the Qurʾān above earlier scripture because it contains what the Messenger brought in previous divine books and adds further merit.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r16.anchor: وتخلل ذلك تنويه بالقرآن وفضله على غيره باشتماله على ما في الكتب الإلهية التي جاء بها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من قبل

IBNASHUR:98:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r17.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR:98:1/r17.claim: Al-Wāḥidī, quoted by Fakhr al-Dīn from his al-Tafsīr al-Basīṭ, calls this verse among the Qurʾān’s hardest in construction and interpretation, saying even leading scholars were baffled; Fakhr says he did not clarify the problem.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r17.anchor: ذكر الفخر عن الواحدي في « التفسير البسيط » له أنه قال : هذه الآية من أصعب ما في القرآن نظما وتفسيرا

IBNASHUR:98:1/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r18.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR:98:1/r18.claim: Fakhr reads the omitted complement of “detached” as their disbelief and “the clear proof” as the Messenger; “until” then implies they leave disbelief at his coming, apparently conflicting with 98:4, where division follows the proof’s arrival.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r18.anchor: وأنا أقول : وجه الإشكال أن تقدير الآية : لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة التي هي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r19.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr adds that actual history shows neither group ever left disbelief, while the subjunctive verb after ḥattā signals a future event even though the Messenger had arrived years earlier and both groups persisted.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r19.anchor: وأن نصب المضارع بعد { حتى } ينادي على أنه منصوب ب ( أنْ ) مضمرة بعد { حتى }

IBNASHUR:98:1/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r20.claim: Given the apparent contradictions, the wording cannot be understood by its surface sense; interpreters either recast the whole statement or figuratively interpret one or more of its terms.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r20.anchor: فوجب صرفه عن ظاهره ، إما بصرف تركيب الخبر عن ظاهر الإخبار

IBNASHUR:98:1/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r21.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr groups the interpretations into five bases: recast the whole sentence; reinterpret munfakkīn; reinterpret its omitted complement; take ḥattā conditionally; or reinterpret rasūl, with some allowing two senses for bayyina. Al-Ālūsī and al-Qurṭubī collect most variants, sometimes without attribution.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r21.anchor: ومراجع تأويل الآية تؤول إلى خمسة : الأول : تأويل الجملة بأسرها

IBNASHUR:98:1/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r22.speaker: الفراء ونفطويه والزمخشري
IBNASHUR:98:1/r22.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, Niftawayh, and al-Zamakhsharī take the whole statement as a rebuke and expression of astonishment.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r22.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب الفراء ونفطويه والزمخشري

IBNASHUR:98:1/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r23.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:98:1/r23.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya interprets munfakkīn as being released from God’s forbearance and brought to account.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r23.anchor: بمعنى الخروج عن إمهال الله إياهم ومصيرهم إلى مؤاخذتهم ، وهو لابن عطية

IBNASHUR:98:1/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r24.speaker: عبد الجبار
IBNASHUR:98:1/r24.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbār supplies “from disbelief” as the omitted complement of munfakkīn.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r24.anchor: بأنه عن الكفر وهو لعبد الجبار

IBNASHUR:98:1/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r25.speaker: الفخر وأبو حيان
IBNASHUR:98:1/r25.claim: Fakhr and Abū Ḥayyān supply “from their agreement in disbelief” as the omitted complement of munfakkīn.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r25.anchor: أو عن الاتفاق على الكفر وهو للفخر وأبي حيان

IBNASHUR:98:1/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r26.speaker: ابن كيسان الأصم
IBNASHUR:98:1/r26.claim: Ibn Kaysān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān known as al-Aṣamm, takes the omitted complement to mean they had not ceased bearing witness to the Messenger’s truth before his mission.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r26.anchor: أو منفكين عن الشهادة للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصدق قبل بعثته وهو لابن كيسان عبد الرحمن الملقب بالأصم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r27.speaker: بعض اللغويين
IBNASHUR:98:1/r27.claim: Some linguists understand munfakkīn as no longer alive, that is, doomed to perish.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r27.anchor: أو منفكين عن الحياة ، أي هالكين ، وعزي إلى بعض اللغويين

IBNASHUR:98:1/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r28.claim: Another interpretation takes ḥattā as the connective conditional particle in, giving the sense “even if the clear proof comes to them.”

IBNASHUR:98:1/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r29.speaker: أبو مسلم
IBNASHUR:98:1/r29.claim: Abū Muslim, as cited by Fakhr, takes rasūl to mean angels sent to read divine scrolls, like the People of the Book’s request in 4:153; this reading makes the statement sarcastic.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r29.anchor: وعزاه الفخر إلى أبي مسلم وهو يقتضي صرف الخبر إلى التهكم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r30.claim: Some commentators allow two interpretations of the word bayyina.

IBNASHUR:98:1/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r31.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r31.claim: The People of the Book described as disbelievers are those who rejected Muḥammad’s message, as in 59:11.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r31.anchor: أنهم كفروا برسالة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r32.claim: These verses argue against unbelieving scripturalists and polytheists who used excuses to persist stubbornly in disbelief; the sentence recounts their claim that they would not leave their religion until the promised sign arrived.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r32.anchor: إن هذه الآيات وردت مورد إقامة الحجة على الذين لم يؤمنوا من أهل الكتاب وعلى المشركين بأنهم متنصلون من الحق متعللون للإصرار على الكفر عنادا

IBNASHUR:98:1/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r33.claim: He treats the report as a compound figurative use of an informative sentence for an utterance act, like using a question for rebuke; al-Taftāzānī says no one has identified its precise figure, while al-Sayyid explains it fully.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r33.anchor: استعمال الخبر في الإنشاء والاستفهام في التوبيخ ونحو ذلك الذي قال فيه التفتزاني

IBNASHUR:98:1/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r34.claim: A close parallel is 9:64: hypocrites were described as fearing exposure, although their apparent fear was pretense, and then told to mock because God would reveal what they hid.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r34.anchor: وقريب منه قوله تعالى : { يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم

IBNASHUR:98:1/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r35.claim: The polytheists excused themselves by saying scripture had been sent only to two earlier communities and that they would have been better guided if they had received one.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r35.anchor: قال تعالى : { أن تقولوا إنما أنزل الكتاب على طائفتين من قبلنا

IBNASHUR:98:1/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r36.claim: The People of the Book also used the excuse that God had covenanted with them not to believe a messenger until he brought a sacrifice consumed by fire.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r36.anchor: الذين قالوا إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار

IBNASHUR:98:1/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r37.claim: Because both groups widely used this excuse, the future “until the proof comes” precisely recalls what they said before the Messenger arrived and exposes it as an argument against them.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r37.anchor: وشيوعه عن الفريقين قرينة على أن المراد من سياقه دمغهم بالحجة وبذلك كان التعبير بالمضارع المستقبل

IBNASHUR:98:1/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r38.claim: Another parallel is 2:89: the People of the Book had sought victory over the disbelievers before the confirming Book came, but rejected what they recognized when it arrived.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r38.anchor: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

IBNASHUR:98:1/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:1/r39.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:1/r39.claim: The intended force is: you used to claim you would not abandon your religion until the promised sign came.
IBNASHUR:98:1/r39.anchor: أنكم كنتم تقولون لا نترك ما نحن عليه من الدين حتى تأتينا البينة

IBNASHUR:98:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r2.claim: Al-infikāk means ceasing or desisting; it is the intransitive counterpart of separating something and is figuratively used for desisting from it.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r2.anchor: فالانفكاك : الإقلاع ، وهو مطاوع فكه إذا فصله وفرقه ويستعار لمعنى أقلع عنه

IBNASHUR:98:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r3.claim: The omitted complement of “desisting” is their disbelief: they would leave it, whether it was associating partners with God or rejecting the Messenger.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r3.anchor: ومتعلق { منفكين } محذوف دل عليه وصف المتحدث عنهم بصلة { الذين كفروا } والتقدير : منفكين عن كفرهم وتاركين له

IBNASHUR:98:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the statement came from Jews in Medina and nearby towns, then reached Meccan polytheists consulting scripturalists for an excuse to avoid blame for rejecting Islam.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r4.anchor: فهذا القول صادر من اليهود الذين في المدينة والقرى التي حولها ويتلقفه المشركون بمكة الذين لم ينقطعوا عن الاتصال بأهل الكتاب

IBNASHUR:98:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r5.claim: The discussion also encompasses Bedouin polytheists around Medina, including Juhayna and Ghatafān, and individual Christians in Mecca or Medina.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r5.anchor: وكذلك المشركون الذين حول المدينة من الأعراب

IBNASHUR:98:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r6.speaker: اليهود
IBNASHUR:98:2/r6.claim: The Jews claimed God had bound them not to believe in a messenger until he brought a sacrifice consumed by fire.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r6.anchor: وقد حكى الله عن اليهود أنهم قالوا : { إن الله عهد إلينا ألا نؤمن لرسول حتى يأتينا بقربان تأكله النار }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r7.speaker: اليهود
IBNASHUR:98:2/r7.claim: The Jews had earlier recognized the promised scripture, sought victory over disbelievers through it, then rejected it when it came to them.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r7.anchor: وقال عنهم : { ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r8.speaker: النصارى
IBNASHUR:98:2/r8.claim: The Christians were described as having rejected Jesus’ announcement of a later messenger named Aḥmad, calling the messenger’s clear signs sorcery.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r8.anchor: وحكى عن النصارى بقوله تعالى حكاية عن عيسى : { ومبشراً برسول يأتي من بعدي اسمه أحمد فلما جاءهم بالبينات قالوا هذا سحر مبين }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r9.speaker: أهل الكتاب
IBNASHUR:98:2/r9.claim: Many People of the Book wished that believers would return to disbelief out of envy after the truth had become clear to them.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r9.anchor: وقال عن الفريقين : { ود كثير من أهل الكتاب لو يردونكم من بعد إيمانكم كفاراً حسداً من عند أنفسهم من بعد ما تبين لهم الحق }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r10.speaker: المشركون
IBNASHUR:98:2/r10.claim: The polytheists demanded a sign like those given to Moses or to earlier messengers.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r10.anchor: وحكى عن المشركين بقوله :  { فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا

IBNASHUR:98:2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says both scriptural communities had been charged to await a prophet who would support the true religion, with signs evident in his mission.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r11.anchor: ولم يختلف أهل الكتابين في أنهم أخذ عليهم العهد بانتظار نبيء ينصر الدين الحق وجعلت علاماته دلائل تظهر من دعوته

IBNASHUR:98:2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r12.speaker: التوراة
IBNASHUR:98:2/r12.claim: Deuteronomy promises a prophet from among the Israelites’ brethren, like Moses, with God’s words placed in his mouth.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r12.anchor: كقول التوراة في سفر التثنية : « أقيم لهم نبيئاً من وسط إخوتهم مثلَك وأجعل كلامي في فمه »

IBNASHUR:98:2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r13.speaker: التوراة
IBNASHUR:98:2/r13.claim: The quoted Deuteronomy passage says a prophet who speaks presumptuously in God’s name and whose prediction fails is not speaking God’s word.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r13.anchor: ثم قولها فيه : « وأما النبي الذي يطغى فيتكلم كلاماً لم أوصه أن يتكلم به فيموت ذلك النبي

IBNASHUR:98:2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the Gospel’s promise that the comforter remains forever as referring to the enduring religious law, since a prophet himself does not live forever.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r14.anchor: أي شريعته لأن ذات النبي لا تمكث إلى الأبد

IBNASHUR:98:2/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r15.speaker: الإنجيل
IBNASHUR:98:2/r15.claim: The Gospel passage promises that the Holy Spirit, sent by the Father in Jesus’ name, will teach the followers everything and remind them of Jesus’ words.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r15.anchor: وأما المعزي الروح القدس الذي سيرسله الأب باسمي فهو يعلمكم كل شيء ويذكركم بكل ما قلتُه لكم

IBNASHUR:98:2/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r16.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr interprets Matthew’s endurance to the end as the persistence of the religion, because no person can remain alive until the world ends.

IBNASHUR:98:2/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r17.speaker: الإنجيل
IBNASHUR:98:2/r17.claim: Matthew says the kingdom’s good news will be proclaimed throughout the inhabited world as testimony to all nations before the end comes.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r17.anchor: ويكرر ببشارة الملكوت هذه في كل المسكونة شهادة لجميع الأمم ثم يأتي المنتهى

IBNASHUR:98:2/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r18.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr takes the worldwide proclamation followed by the end as indicating that the promised messenger is the final messenger.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r18.anchor: فهو خاتم الرسل كما هو بين

IBNASHUR:98:2/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r19.claim: Jewish religious scholars misinterpreted prophecies about the coming messenger and invented imaginary identifying signs; later generations awaited those inventions and denied the envoy when he lacked them.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r19.anchor: وكان أحبارهم قد أساءوا التأويل للبشارات الواردة في كتبهم بالرسول المقفي وأدخلوا علامات يعرفون بها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم الموعود به هي من المخترعات الموهومة

IBNASHUR:98:2/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r20.claim: Al-bayyina means a clear proof and a sign of truth; its feminine form is understood as standing for testimony or a sign.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r20.anchor: و { البينة } : الحجة الواضحة والعلامة على الصدق وهو اسم منقول من الوصف جرى على التأنيث لأنه مؤول بالشهادة أو الآية

IBNASHUR:98:2/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r21.claim: The word bayyina is apt because it renders the scriptural idea of clear testimony, such as Matthew’s phrase “testimony to all nations”; its two occurrences may reflect that specificity.

IBNASHUR:98:2/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r22.claim: He connects the proof and the earlier scriptures with the verse asking whether the sign of what was in the former scriptures had not come to them.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r22.anchor: وقد ذكرت مع ذكر الصحف الأولى في قوله : { وقالوا لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أو لم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى }

IBNASHUR:98:2/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r23.claim: The apparent reading takes the definite article as generic mental definiteness: a known kind of proof, not one individually specified proof, like saying “enter the market.”
IBNASHUR:98:2/r23.anchor: والظاهر أن التعريف في { البينة } تعريف العهد الذهني ، وهو أن يراد معهود بنوعه لا بشخصه كقولهم : ادخل السوق

IBNASHUR:98:2/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r24.speaker: علماء البلاغة
IBNASHUR:98:2/r24.claim: Rhetoricians say a noun defined by this generic al has an indefinite sense in meaning.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r24.anchor: ولذلك قال علماء البلاغة : إن المعرف بهذه اللام هو في المعنى نكرة فكأنه قيل حتى تأتيهم بينة

IBNASHUR:98:2/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r25.claim: Alternatively, the article may refer to a proof already familiar to the addressed communities—the prophetic instructions they expected, though each imagined them differently.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r25.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التعريف لمعهود عند المخبر عنهم ، أي البينة التي هي وصايا أنبيائهم فهي معهودة عند كل فريق منهم وإن اختلفوا في تخيلها

IBNASHUR:98:2/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r26.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses bayyina language for this kind of proof, including the clear proof in earlier scriptures, clear signs rejected as sorcery, truth made clear, and the Qur’an’s clarifications.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r26.anchor: وأوثرت كلمة { البينة } لأنها تعبر عن المعنى الوارد في كلامهم ولذلك نرى مادتها متكررة في آيات كثيرة من القرآن في هذا الغرض

IBNASHUR:98:2/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r27.claim: In “from the People of the Book,” min is explanatory, clarifying which disbelievers are meant.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r27.anchor: و { من } في قوله : { من أهل الكتاب } بيانية بيان للذين كفروا

IBNASHUR:98:2/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:2/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:2/r28.claim: People of the Book precede the polytheists despite the latter’s graver disbelief because they first circulated the supposed proof among them and supplied more sophisticated objections; the initial refutation targets them, with polytheists following.
IBNASHUR:98:2/r28.anchor: وإنما قدم أهل الكتاب على المشركين هنا مع أن كفر المشركين أشد من كفر أهل الكتاب لأن لأهل الكتاب السبق في هذا المقام

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r1.claim: Most commentators classify the sūra as Meccan, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya says is the better-known view.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية في قول جمهور المفسرين ،   وقال ابن الزبير ،   وعطاء : هي مدنية ،   والأول أشهر

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير وعطاء
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAṭāʾ classify the sūra as Medinan.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير ،   وعطاء : هي مدنية

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex reads mā kāna alladhīna in place of lam yakun alladhīna.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r3.anchor: وفي حرف أبي بن كعب : «ما كان الذين »

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex reads lam yakun al-mushrikīn wa-ahl al-kitāb munfakkīn.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r4.anchor: وفي حرف ابن مسعود : «لم يكن المشركين وأهل الكتاب منفكين »

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r5.claim: Munfakkīn means separated or dispersed; the idiom describes one thing separating from another.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r5.anchor: تقول : انفك الشيء عن الشيء إذا انفصل عنه

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r6.claim: The phrase mā انفك, as a defective verb among kāna’s sisters, has no role in this verse.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r6.anchor: وما انفك التي هي من أخوات كان لا مدخل بها في هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r7.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r7.claim: Mujāhid and others say they would not leave disbelief and error until the clear sign came.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r7.anchor: فقال مجاهد وغيره : لم يكونوا { منفكين } عن الكفر والضلال حتى جاءتهم البينة

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the future verb taʾtīhim stands where a past form would, since the verse’s main remainder was not yet intended as past.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r8.anchor: وأوقع المستقبل موضع الماضي في { تأتيهم } ،   لأن باقي الآية وعظمها لم يرده بعد

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r9.speaker: الفراء وغيره
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others say they did not cease recognizing the truth of Muhammad’s prophethood and attending to his cause until the sign came, whereupon they split.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء وغيره : لم يكونوا { منفكين } عن معرفة صحة نبوة محمد عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r10.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r10.claim: Some grammarians parse munfakkīn with the defective verb mā انفك and posit an omitted predicate such as knowing Muhammad’s affair.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r10.anchor: وذهب بعض النحويين إلى هذا النفي المتقدم مع { منفكين } يجعلها تلك التي هي مع كان

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors a third reading: the people remained under God’s command, power, and care until He sent a warner to establish proof and complete blessing for believers; they were not left neglected.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r11.anchor: لم يكن هؤلاء القوم { منفكين } من أمر الله تعالى وقدرته ونظره لهم

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r12.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r12.claim: Some read al-mushrikūn in the nominative.

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r13.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r13.claim: The majority read al-mushrikīn in the genitive; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the meanings are clear.

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r14.claim: Al-bayyina means the clear and manifest account or event.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r14.anchor: و { البينة } معناه : القصة البينة والجلية ،   والمراد محمد عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA:98:1/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r15.claim: The clear sign refers to Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA:98:1/r15.anchor: و { البينة } معناه : القصة البينة والجلية ،   والمراد محمد عليه السلام

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr identifies Sūrat al-Bayyina as Medinan.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r1.anchor: تفسير سورة لم يكن وهي مدنية

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r2.speaker: أبو حية البدري
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayya al-Badrī reports Gabriel told the Prophet that God commanded him to recite this sūra to Ubayy; Ubayy asked whether he had been named and wept.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا حَيَّة البدري - وهو : مالك بن عمرو بن ثابت الأنصاري

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r3.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said God ordered him to recite this sūra to Ubayy and had named Ubayy; Ubayy wept. Bukhārī, Muslim, Tirmidhī and Nasāʾī transmit it.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب :

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r4.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet's order to recite a sūra to him, asks whether he was mentioned there, then rejoices and cites God’s command to rejoice in His bounty and mercy; this route is unique to Aḥmad.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r4.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r5.claim: In another report, Ubayy says the Prophet recited the Qur’an to him, including sayings on human desire for wealth, repentance, and the true hanīf religion; Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r5.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش ، عن أبي بن كعب قال : إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لي :

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r6.claim: A rare al-Ṭabarānī route has Ubayy ask whether he was mentioned; the Prophet says Ubayy was named with lineage in the highest assembly. Ibn Kathīr says the earlier reports are established.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r7.claim: Ubayy reports that the Prophet affirmed both his and Ibn Masʿūd’s readings, then explained Gabriel’s successive permission for the community to recite on up to seven aḥruf.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r7.anchor: كان قد أنكر على إنسان ، وهو : عبد الله بن مسعود ، قراءة شيء من القرآن

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r8.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the Prophet recited the sūra to Ubayy to affirm, strengthen and warn him, not to teach or review it with him.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r8.anchor: قرأها عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قراءة إبلاغ وتثبيت وإنذار ، لا قراءة تعلم واستذكار

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr compares this to Ḥudaybiyya: after Umar asked about the promised pilgrimage, the Prophet clarified its timing, then read Sūrat al-Fatḥ, including the promise in 48:27.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r9.anchor: وفيها قوله : { لَقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامِ

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r10.claim: Ibn Kathīr transmits through Abū Nuʿaym and Fuḍayl the Prophet’s promise of Paradise to a reciter of this sūra until satisfied, and calls the report extremely rare.

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r11.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Madīnī and Ibn al-Athīr transmit a variant through al-Zuhrī and Naẓīr (or Nadhīr) al-Muzanī/al-Madanī: God will never forget the reciter and will satisfy him in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r11.anchor: عن نظير المزني - أو : المدني - عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r12.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are worshippers of idols and fire, Arab and non-Arab.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r12.anchor: أما أهل الكتاب فهم : اليهود والنصارى ، والمشركون : عَبَدةُ الأوثان والنيران ، من العرب ومن العجم

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r13.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r13.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda gloss “not desisting” as their not stopping until the truth became clear to them.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد : لم يكونوا { مُنْفَكِّينَ } يعني : منتهين حتى يتبين لهم الحق . وكذا قال قتادة

IBNKATHIR:98:1/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r14.claim: Ibn Kathīr identifies the clear proof that came to them as the Qur’an.
IBNKATHIR:98:1/r14.anchor: أي : هذا القرآن ؛ ولهذا قال تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir conjectures that the doubt Ubay experienced prompted the Prophet to recite Surah al-Bayyinah to him as reassurance, since it includes the Messenger reciting purified pages containing upright books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: قلت: وهذا الشك الذي حصل لأبي في تلك الساعة هو، والله أعلم، السبب الذي لأجله قرأ عليه رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: As a parallel, the Prophet recited al-Fath to Umar after Hudaybiya because Umar had questioned the promise that Muslims would enter the Sacred Mosque safely.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: وهذا نظير تلاوته سورة الفتح حين أنزلت مرجعه، عليه السلام، من الحديبية على عمر بن الخطاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: Ubay reports Gabriel successively instructed the Prophet to recite in one, two, three, then seven ahruf; he repeatedly sought ease because his community could not bear fewer options, and at seven Gabriel said every reading they used was correct.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان عند أخباة بني غفار، فأتاه جبريل فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: Abu Dawud’s wording says the seven forms are each healing and sufficient, including synonymous divine attributes such as All-Hearing/All-Knowing or Mighty/Wise, but a verse of punishment must not be ended with mercy or vice versa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor: وفي لفظ لأبي داود عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يا أبي، إني أقرئت القرآن

KASHSHAF:98:1/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan according to one view and Medinan according to another; it has eight verses.

KASHSHAF:98:1/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r2.claim: Before Muḥammad’s mission, the People of the Book and idol-worshippers said they would not leave their religions until the promised prophet named in the Torah and Gospel—Muḥammad—came.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r2.anchor: كان الكفار من الفريقين أهل الكتاب وعبدة الأصنام يقولون قبل مبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا ننفك مما نحن عليه من ديننا

KASHSHAF:98:1/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r3.claim: The quotation is reproachful: they expected to unite on truth when the Messenger came, yet his coming was what divided the People of the Book from truth and confirmed their disbelief.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r3.anchor: ثم قال : { وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب } يعني أنهم كانوا يعدون اجتماع الكلمة والاتفاق على الحق : إذا جاءهم الرسول ،

KASHSHAF:98:1/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r4.claim: The author illustrates the reproach with a sinful poor man who promises to leave vice when made rich, then becomes worse; the adviser exposes the contradiction to rebuke and bind him to his words.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r4.anchor: ونظيره في الكلام أن يقول الفقير الفاسق لمن يعظه : لست بمنفك مما أنا فيه حتى يرزقني الله الغنى ،

KASHSHAF:98:1/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r5.claim: “Infikāk” is separation after close attachment, like a bone coming out of its joint.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r5.anchor: وانفكاك الشيء من الشيء أن يزايله بعد التحامه به ، كالعظم إذا انفك من مفصله ؛ والمعنى : أنهم متشبثون

KASHSHAF:98:1/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r6.claim: The people were clinging to their religion and would not leave it until the clear proof arrived.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r6.anchor: والمعنى : أنهم متشبثون بدينهم لا يتركونه إلا عند مجيء البينة .

KASHSHAF:98:1/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:1/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:1/r7.claim: “The clear proof” means an unmistakable argument.
KASHSHAF:98:1/r7.anchor: لا يتركونه إلا عند مجيء البينة . و { البينة } الحجة الواضحة .

MAWARDI:98:1/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:98:1/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām says the sūra is Meccan.
MAWARDI:98:1/r1.anchor: سورة البينة مكية في قول يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:98:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r2.claim: The majority classify the sūra as Medinan, and al-Māwardī says this is correct.

MAWARDI:98:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r3.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the polytheists are Arab idol-worshippers and others who have no scripture.
MAWARDI:98:1/r3.anchor: من اليهود والنصارى الذين هم أهل الكتاب ، ولم يكن المشركون الذين هم عبدة الأوثان

MAWARDI:98:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r4.claim: Munfakkīn may mean that they would not stop associating partners with God until the proof made truth clear.
MAWARDI:98:1/r4.anchor: أحدها : لم يكونوا منتهين عن الشرك { حتى تأتيهم البينة } حتى يتبين لهم الحق

MAWARDI:98:1/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r5.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI:98:1/r5.claim: They remained in polytheism and doubt until the clear proof came, meaning the messengers.
MAWARDI:98:1/r5.anchor: وهذا قول ثان : لم يزالوا مقيمين على الشرك والريبة حتى تأتيهم البينة ، يعني الرسل ، قاله الربيع

MAWARDI:98:1/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r6.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:98:1/r6.claim: They had not split over whether God would send them a messenger until Muhammad came; then some believed and others disbelieved.
MAWARDI:98:1/r6.anchor: أن الله سيبعث إليهم رسولا حتى بعث الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فاختلفوا وتفرقوا ، فمنهم من آمن بربه ، ومنهم من كفر ، قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI:98:1/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r7.claim: They could not escape God’s proofs until the clear proof established the case against them; Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse illustrates the usage of anfakka for ceasing.
MAWARDI:98:1/r7.anchor: الرابع : لم يكونوا ليتركوا منفكين من حجج الله تعالى ، حتى تأتيهم البينة التي تقوم بها عليهم الحجة ، قال امرؤ القيس

MAWARDI:98:1/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:98:1/r8.claim: Al-Qatāda identifies the clear proof as the Qurʾān.
MAWARDI:98:1/r8.anchor: وفي " البينة " ها هنا ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : القرآن ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:98:1/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r9.claim: Another view identifies the clear proof as the Messenger, whose signs of prophethood are manifest.
MAWARDI:98:1/r9.anchor: الرسول الذي بانت فيه دلائل النبوة

MAWARDI:98:1/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI:98:1/r10.claim: A third view takes the clear proof as the clarification of truth and the appearance of proofs.

MAWARDI:98:1/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MAWARDI:98:1/r11.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads mā kāna in place of lam yakun and singularizes alladhī.
MAWARDI:98:1/r11.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب : ما كان الذي كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين

MAWARDI:98:1/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:1/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI:98:1/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the clause with the polytheists before the People of the Book.
MAWARDI:98:1/r12.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين

NASAFI:98:1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r1.claim: The sura's place of revelation is disputed, and Nasafi counts eight verses.
NASAFI:98:1/r1.anchor: سورة البينة مختلف فيها ،   وهى ثماني آيات

NASAFI:98:1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r2.claim: Those who disbelieved in Muhammad among the People of the Book are Jews and Christians; the People of a man are his closest kin.
NASAFI:98:1/r2.anchor: بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { مّنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب } أي اليهود والنصارى ، وأهل الرجل أخص الناس به

NASAFI:98:1/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r3.claim: People of Islam are those who profess it.
NASAFI:98:1/r3.anchor: وأهل الإسلام من يدين به { والمشركين } عبدة الأصنام

NASAFI:98:1/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r4.anchor: وأهل الإسلام من يدين به { والمشركين } عبدة الأصنام

NASAFI:98:1/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r5.claim: They were not separated from disbelief.
NASAFI:98:1/r5.anchor: { والمشركين } عبدة الأصنام { مُنفَكِّينَ } منفصلين عن الكفر

NASAFI:98:1/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r6.claim: The complement of “separated” is omitted because the relative clause “who disbelieved” makes it clear.

NASAFI:98:1/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:1/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:1/r7.claim: The clear proof is Muhammad; after he came, some accepted Islam and others remained disbelievers.
NASAFI:98:1/r7.anchor: والمراد محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، يقول : لم يتركوا كفرهم حتى يبعث محمد

QURTUBI:98:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r1.speaker: يحيي بن سلام وابن عباس والجمهور
QURTUBI:98:1/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam calls the sura Meccan, while Ibn Abbas and most scholars call it Medinan; it has nine verses.
QURTUBI:98:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية في قول يحيي بن سلام ، ومدنية  في قول ابن عباس والجمهور . وهي تسع

QURTUBI:98:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:98:1/r2.claim: A report promising immense rewards for learning this sura says people would abandon family and wealth to learn it, that angels recite it continually, and that reciters receive angelic protection and prayers; Qurtubi says the report is unsound, and Ibn al-Arabi calls its version false.

QURTUBI:98:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:98:1/r3.claim: In the sound report from Anas, God ordered the Prophet to recite this sura to Ubayy ibn Ka'b; when Ubayy asked whether God had named him, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept. Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
QURTUBI:98:1/r3.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب

QURTUBI:98:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r4.claim: Qurtubi draws a legal lesson from the report: a teacher may recite to a learner.
QURTUBI:98:1/r4.anchor: وفيه من الفقه قراءة العالم على المتعلم

QURTUBI:98:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r5.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:98:1/r5.claim: Some say the Prophet recited to Ubayy to teach humility, so no one would disdain learning from or reading to someone lower in rank.
QURTUBI:98:1/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : إنما قرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أبي ، ليعلم الناس التواضع ؛ لئلا يأنف أحد من التعلم والقراءة على من دونه في المنزلة .

QURTUBI:98:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r6.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:98:1/r6.claim: Another view says Ubayy learned the Prophet's wording especially quickly, so the Prophet recited to him for exact transmission and to enable him to teach others.
QURTUBI:98:1/r6.anchor: وقيل : لأن أبيا كان أسرع أخذا لألفاظ رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:98:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:98:1/r7.claim: A statement about Adam's greed for wealth, death filling his belly, and God's acceptance of repentance was attributed to Ubayy's reading of this sura.
QURTUBI:98:1/r7.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش قال في قراءة أبي بن كعب : ابن آدم لو أعطي واديا من مال لالتمس ثانيا

QURTUBI:98:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r8.speaker: أبو بكر الأنباري
QURTUBI:98:1/r8.claim: Abu Bakr al-Anbari says this addition is false as Qur'an: the connected readings of Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, both traced to Ubayy, omit it; it is known as the Prophet's speech, not God's Qur'an, and consensus outweighs one contrary report.
QURTUBI:98:1/r8.anchor: قال أبو بكر : هذا باطل عند أهل العلم ، لأن قراءتي ابن كثير وأبي عمرو متصلتان بأبي بن كعب ، لا يقرأ فيها هذا المذكور

QURTUBI:98:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r9.claim: The public reading and the consonantal text of the codex have lam yakun alladhina kafaru.
QURTUBI:98:1/r9.anchor: قوله تعالى : { لم يكن الذين كفروا } كذا قراءة العامة ، وخط المصحف .

QURTUBI:98:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:98:1/r10.claim: Ibn Masud's wording, the polytheists and People of the Book did not cease, is an explanatory reading rather than a recitation; Ibn al-Arabi allows it for exposition only, since recitation is what the codex contains.
QURTUBI:98:1/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود " لم يكن المشركون وأهل الكتاب منفكين " وهذه قراءة على التفسير .

QURTUBI:98:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r11.claim: Ahl al-Kitab means Jews and Christians; al-mushrikin is genitive, coordinated with Ahl al-Kitab.
QURTUBI:98:1/r11.anchor: قوله تعالى : { من أهل الكتاب } يعني اليهود والنصارى { والمشركين } في موضع جر عطفا على { أهل الكتاب } .

QURTUBI:98:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:98:1/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the People of the Book as the Jews of Yathrib—Qurayza, Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa—and the polytheists as Quraysh in Mecca and its vicinity.
QURTUBI:98:1/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس { أهل الكتاب } : اليهود الذين كانوا بيثرب ، وهم قريظة والنضير وبنو قينقاع .

QURTUBI:98:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r13.claim: Munfakkin means ceasing from disbelief or turning away from it.

QURTUBI:98:1/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r14.claim: Qurtubi explains the wording until the clear proof comes as until the clear proof came, referring to Muhammad.
QURTUBI:98:1/r14.anchor: أي أتتهم البينة ، أي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم .

QURTUBI:98:1/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r15.claim: One explanation takes infikak as reaching an endpoint: they would not reach the end of their lives and die until the clear proof came.
QURTUBI:98:1/r15.anchor: وقيل : الانتهاء بلوغ الغاية ، أي لم يكونوا ليبلغوا نهاية أعمارهم فيموتوا ، حتى تأتيهم البينة

QURTUBI:98:1/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r16.claim: Another gloss is vanishing: their allotted time would not expire until a messenger came.
QURTUBI:98:1/r16.anchor: أي لم تكن مدتهم لتزول حتى يأتيهم رسول .

QURTUBI:98:1/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r17.claim: The root f-k-k carries the sense of opening or separating; Arab idiom ما انفككت أفعل and ما انفك فلان قائما means continuing or remaining.
QURTUBI:98:1/r17.anchor: الفك : الفتح ،   ومنه فك الكتاب ، وفك الخلخال

QURTUBI:98:1/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r18.claim: Another gloss is departing: they would not leave and pass from the world until the clear proof came.
QURTUBI:98:1/r18.anchor: بارحين ، أي لم يكونوا ليبرحوا ويفارقوا الدنيا ، حتى تأتيهم البينة .

QURTUBI:98:1/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r19.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI:98:1/r19.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the People of the Book retained descriptions of Muhammad in their scriptures until his mission, then envied and denied him, as in 2:89 and 98:4.
QURTUBI:98:1/r19.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان : أي لم يكن أهل الكتاب تاركين صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في كتابهم

QURTUBI:98:1/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r20.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI:98:1/r20.claim: On Ibn Kaysan's reading, the Meccan polytheists called Muhammad al-Amin and did not speak ill of him until the clear proof came and they opposed him.
QURTUBI:98:1/r20.anchor: وعلى هذا { والمشركين } أي ما كانوا يسيئون القول في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، حتى بعث

QURTUBI:98:1/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r21.speaker: بعض اللغويين
QURTUBI:98:1/r21.claim: Some linguists derive munfakkin from a woman's pelvic bone separating during childbirth and failing to reunite; the verse then means they are not punished or destroyed until messengers and books establish proof.
QURTUBI:98:1/r21.anchor: وقال بعض اللغويين :  " منفكين "  هالكين من قولهم : انفك صلا

QURTUBI:98:1/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r22.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI:98:1/r22.claim: One view includes the polytheists among the People of the Book, citing Jews who called Ezra God's son and Christians who called Jesus God, His son, or one of three.
QURTUBI:98:1/r22.anchor: وقال قوم في المشركين : إنهم من أهل الكتاب

QURTUBI:98:1/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r23.claim: Another view distinguishes them by history: the People of the Book believed before disbelieving after their prophets, while polytheists began in natural disposition and disbelieved upon maturity.
QURTUBI:98:1/r23.anchor: وقيل : أهل الكتاب كانوا مؤمنين ، ثم كفروا بعد أنبيائهم . والمشركون ولدوا على الفطرة

QURTUBI:98:1/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r24.claim: Another view takes polytheists as a description of the People of the Book too: they abandoned monotheism and their scriptures, since Christians are trinitarian and most Jews anthropomorphists; all are shirk.
QURTUBI:98:1/r24.anchor: وقيل : المشركون وصف أهل الكتاب أيضا ، لأنهم لم ينتفعوا بكتابهم ، وتركوا التوحيد .

QURTUBI:98:1/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:1/r25.claim: Another interpretation restricts disbelief to rejection of Muhammad: the People of the Book are Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are idol worshippers without scripture.
QURTUBI:98:1/r25.anchor: وقيل : إن الكفر هنا هو الكفر بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أي لم يكن الذين كفروا بمحمد

QURTUBI:98:1/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r26.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI:98:1/r26.claim: Al-Qushayri finds that interpretation strained because the following phrase identifies the clear proof as Muhammad; it can work only if it means they persisted in present disbelief until Muhammad came, explained the signs, and some then believed.
QURTUBI:98:1/r26.anchor: قال القشيري : وفيه بعد ؛ لأن الظاهر من { حتى تأتيهم البينة . رسول من الله } أن هذا الرسول هو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:98:1/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r27.speaker: الأعمش وإبراهيم
QURTUBI:98:1/r27.claim: Al-A'mash and Ibrahim read al-mushrikun in the nominative, coordinated with alladhina; Qurtubi prefers the genitive reading because nominative makes both groups seem outside the People of the Book.
QURTUBI:98:1/r27.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وإبراهيم " والمشركون " رفعا ، عطفا على

QURTUBI:98:1/r28.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:1/r28.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:98:1/r28.claim: Ubayy's codex has the variant فما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركون منفكين.
QURTUBI:98:1/r28.anchor: وفي حرف أبيّ : " فما كان الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركون منفكين "

RAZI:98:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:98:1/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls this one of the Qur'an's hardest verses in structure and interpretation, saying major scholars struggled with it.
RAZI:98:1/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط : هذه الآية من أصعب ما في القرآن

RAZI:98:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r2.claim: The apparent problem is that 98:1 seems to say they left disbelief when the Messenger came, while 98:4 says the People of Scripture divided only after the proof arrived.
RAZI:98:1/r2.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين حتى تأتيهم البينة

RAZI:98:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r3.claim: Preferring al-Kashshāf's solution, al-Rāzī reads the first clause as the unbelievers' claim that they would not leave their religions until the promised Prophet, Muhammad, came; the next clause reports that his coming instead divided them from truth.
RAZI:98:1/r3.anchor: وهو أن الكفار من الفريقين أهل الكتاب وعبدة الأوثان

RAZI:98:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r4.claim: The poor sinner analogy shows how a preacher can quote someone's earlier condition as a rebuke: he claimed he would reform when wealthy, then grew more sinful after gaining wealth.
RAZI:98:1/r4.anchor: أن يقول الفقير الفاسق لمن يعظه : لست أمتنع مما أنا فيه

RAZI:98:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r5.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:98:1/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī construes the clause as saying they would not leave disbelief even if the proof came; al-Rāzī rejects this because hatta does not mean 'even if' in Arabic.
RAZI:98:1/r5.anchor: ذكره القاضي إلا أن تفسير لفظة حتى بهذا ليس من اللغة في شيء

RAZI:98:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r6.claim: Another proposed reading takes munfakkīn as continuing to praise and mention Muhammad's virtues until the proof came; after his arrival they split and spoke badly of him.
RAZI:98:1/r6.anchor: على الكفر بل على كونهم منفكين عن ذكر محمد بالمناقب والفضائل

RAZI:98:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r7.speaker: ابن عرفة
RAZI:98:1/r7.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says the wording uses the present form but has past meaning, until the proof came, as in 2:102.
RAZI:98:1/r7.anchor: قال ابن عرفة : أي حتى أتتهم

RAZI:98:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r8.claim: The praise-then-rejection reading parallels 2:89, where people previously sought victory through revelation but rejected what they recognized when it came.
RAZI:98:1/r8.anchor: وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

RAZI:98:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī explicitly selects the first explanation: the clause reports what the unbelievers claimed, whereas the following clause reports what actually happened.
RAZI:98:1/r9.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين } عن كفرهم

RAZI:98:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r10.claim: A fourth solution says the collective group did not leave disbelief before the Messenger, but afterward it changed because some believed and others persisted in disbelief.
RAZI:98:1/r10.anchor: حكم على الكفار أنهم ما كانوا منفكين عن كفرهم إلى وقت مجيء الرسول

RAZI:98:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r11.claim: A fifth solution says they had been certain of their inherited religions before Muhammad, but his coming unsettled them into doubt and confusion; munfakkīn suggests separation from certainty.
RAZI:98:1/r11.anchor: كانوا قبل مبعث الرسول منفكين عن التردد في كفرهم بل كانوا جازمين به معتقدين حقيقته

RAZI:98:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r12.claim: The unbelievers are two groups: People of Scripture, Jews and Christians who introduced unbelief into their religion, and polytheists who had no scripture.
RAZI:98:1/r12.anchor: الكفار كانوا جنسين ( أحدهما ) : أهل الكتاب كفرق اليهود والنصارى

RAZI:98:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r13.claim: One solution to the apparent partitive sense of min is to read it as explanatory, as in the command to shun the abomination of idols in 22:30.
RAZI:98:1/r13.anchor: كلمة من ههنا ليست للتبعيض بل للتبيين

RAZI:98:1/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r14.claim: Alternatively, min identifies the two sources of those who disbelieved in Muhammad: some were People of Scripture and some polytheists.
RAZI:98:1/r14.anchor: أن الذين كفروا بمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام ، بعضهم من أهل الكتاب

RAZI:98:1/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r15.claim: A third analysis treats al-mushrikīn as a second descriptor of the People of Scripture: Christians are trinitarian and most Jews anthropomorphists, both forms of shirk.
RAZI:98:1/r15.anchor: وصفا لأهل الكتاب ، وذلك لأن النصارى مثلثة واليهود عامتهم مشبهة

RAZI:98:1/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r16.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI:98:1/r16.claim: Some scholars include the Magians among the People of Scripture, citing the Prophetic instruction to treat them by the rules applied to that community.
RAZI:98:1/r16.anchor: ذكر بعض العلماء أنهم داخلون في أهل الكتاب لقوله عليه السلام : «سنوليهم سنة أهل الكتاب

RAZI:98:1/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r17.speaker: الآخرون
RAZI:98:1/r17.claim: Others exclude the Magians, arguing that the verse concerns the Arab communities and that 6:156 identifies only Jews and Christians as the two earlier scriptural groups.
RAZI:98:1/r17.anchor: وأنكره الآخرون قال : لأنه تعالى إنما ذكر من الكفار من كان في بلاد العرب

RAZI:98:1/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r18.claim: Although conjunction does not establish order, the People of Scripture are placed first because the sura is Medinan, they knew scripture and were more culpable for rejecting Muhammad, others followed them, and they held higher status.
RAZI:98:1/r18.anchor: أن السورة مدنية فكأن أهل الكتاب هم المقصودون بالذكر

RAZI:98:1/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:1/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:98:1/r19.claim: Calling them People of Scripture rather than naming Jews and Christians can honor them by their learning, or highlight that their learning makes their unbelief more blameworthy and punishable.
RAZI:98:1/r19.anchor: يدل على كونهم علماء ، وذلك يقتضي إما مزيد تعظيم
